---
title: Opinion Memory Type as a Free-String Addition; Confidence Becomes a Retrieval-Ranking Input
status: accepted
date: 2026-07-22
audience: wakil design
---

# Opinion Memory Type as a Free-String Addition; Confidence Becomes a Retrieval-Ranking Input

## Context

A third-party proposal (`docs/memory-opinion-and-register.md`, never
committed) identified two real gaps in memory extraction: value judgments
and interpretations were being tagged `fact` for lack of a better type, and
casually-asserted 1:1 claims ("hot takes") had no way to be marked as
lower-commitment than a confidently-stated fact.

The proposal's own framing overstated what two existing mechanisms already
did for the hot-take case. Lifecycle `state` does no new work here: every
memory lands in `candidate` unconditionally at ingest
(`src/wakil/app/ingest_service.py`), and only a human `wakil memory
promote|reject|archive` ever changes it — nothing about a memory's type or
confidence has ever influenced that. And `confidence`
(`CandidateMemoryModel.confidence`, `Memory.confidence`) was, before this
change, write-only and display-only: `search_memories()`
(`src/wakil/storage/fts.py`) never even `SELECT`ed the column, and
`retrieval_rank()`/`_ranked_memory_hits()`
(`src/wakil/app/memory_service.py`, `src/wakil/app/search_service.py`) never
read it. So "confidence models hot-take-ness" was aspirational until it was
actually wired into ranking.

`Memory.memory_type` is `String(30)` with no DB enum or CHECK constraint
(`src/wakil/storage/schema.py`), and ADR 0005 already established the
precedent of adding new `memory_type` values (`event`) to that free-string
column with no migration, reusing the existing Memory lifecycle rather than
forking a new one.

## Decision

- `opinion` is added to `CandidateMemoryModel.type`'s `Field` description
  vocabulary — a free-string value addition on an already-free-string
  column, requiring no migration, following the same pattern ADR 0005
  established for `memory_type='event'`.
- `CandidateMemoryModel.confidence` gains `Field(ge=0.0, le=1.0)` —
  previously unconstrained at both the Pydantic and DB layer, tightened
  because its semantic weight (a probability-like scale used to signal
  low-commitment claims) just increased.
- `confidence` becomes a ranking input for the first time:
  `search_memories()` now selects it, and `retrieval_rank()` /
  `_ranked_memory_hits()` use it as a same-state tiebreak — added as a
  fractional offset that never crosses a `_STATE_RANK` boundary, so a
  low-confidence `durable` memory still outranks every `candidate` memory.
  Memories with `confidence IS NULL` (most existing rows, since the field
  was inert before this change) are treated as neutral (`0.5`) for ranking
  purposes, so the existing untagged corpus isn't reshuffled on day one.
- Lifecycle `state` is explicitly **unchanged** by this work: promotion,
  rejection, and archival remain 100% manual via `wakil memory
  promote|reject|archive`; no automatic state transition is introduced
  based on type or confidence. The extractor's `≤0.4` confidence guidance
  for hot takes (`src/wakil/skills/transcript/SKILL.md`) is prompt-only, not
  enforced in code — matching the existing precedent that
  `_clamp01()` (`src/wakil/app/ingest_service.py`) already accepts any
  in-range value without further validation.

## Consequences

- No migration: `memory_type` and `confidence` are both already
  unconstrained-shape columns; `opinion` rows work with every existing
  filter (`wakil memory list --type opinion`) and display path unmodified.
- `state` remains the sole durability signal a human controls directly;
  `confidence` only ever reorders memories that already share a state, and
  never determines durability itself.
- The fact/opinion boundary (especially unestablished causal "because"
  clauses) is judgment-call territory for the extractor model and is not
  perfectly consistent across ingests — covered by a new
  `src/wakil/skills/transcript/eval.json` scenario
  (`hypothesis-vs-opinion-because-clause`) rather than a hard rule, per ADR
  0004's live-model eval gating.
- An explicit `register`/`stance` field (the proposal's "phase 2") remains
  deferred; ship this first and revisit only if confidence + state prove
  insufficient in practice.

## Sources

- `src/wakil/llm/schemas.py` (`CandidateMemoryModel`)
- `src/wakil/app/memory_service.py` (`retrieval_rank`)
- `src/wakil/storage/fts.py` (`search_memories`)
- `docs/adr/0005-timeline-entries-as-memory-rows.md` (free-string
  `memory_type` precedent)
- `docs/memory-opinion-and-register.md` (originating, non-authoritative
  proposal)

Base directory for this skill: /Users/ebridges/Projects/wakil/.claude/skills/commit

# commit

Group the working tree's pending changes into one or more **logical change sets** and
create a commit for each, with a Conventional Commits message prefixed by a relevant
emoji.

Having a coherent history of logical changes implemented in sequence is a core value
of this system. As a result, you must analyze the working tree's pending changes to
group them appropriately. **Failing to do this analysis and decomposition of the changes
is a violation of a core value of the system**.

## When to use

The user asks to "commit", "commit these changes", "split into logical commits",
"commit in change sets", or similar. Default to this behavior whenever committing.

## Procedure

1. **Survey the changes.** Run these in parallel:
   - `git status --porcelain=v1` — see staged, unstaged, and untracked files.
   - `git diff` and `git diff --staged` — understand _what_ changed, not just which files.
   - `git log --oneline -10` — match the repo's existing message style/scopes.
   - `git branch --show-current` — if on the default branch (`main`/`master`) and the
     user has not said to commit there, branch first or ask.

2. **Group into logical change sets.** Each commit should be one coherent, reviewable
   unit — a single concern that leaves the tree in a working state. Split by intent, not
   by file. Guidelines:
   - One feature, fix, refactor, or doc change per commit.
   - Keep production code and its tests together when they form one change.
   - Separate unrelated concerns even if they touch the same file (use `git add -p` to
     stage hunks selectively when needed).
   - Put pure formatting/lint noise in its own commit, apart from behavioral changes.
   - Order commits so each one builds/passes on its own where practical.
   - If everything is genuinely one concern, a single commit is correct — don't
     manufacture splits.

3. **Check development-docs.** Apply the `development-docs` skill's judgment: does anything from this
   session belong in `docs/DEVELOPMENT.md` or `docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md`? Default is no —
   only add an entry if it clearly clears that skill's bar. If so, fold the doc edit into
   one of the change sets below rather than treating it as a separate follow-up.

4. **Confirm the plan.** Briefly list the proposed commits (message + files) and let the
   user adjust before committing, unless they've said to just do it.

5. **Stage and commit each set.** For each change set: stage exactly its files/hunks
   (`git add <paths>` or `git add -p`), then commit. Verify with `git status` between
   commits that you're only including the intended files. Never `git add -A` blindly when
   splitting.

6. **Report.** Show the resulting `git log --oneline` for the new commits.

## Message format

```
<emoji> <type>(<optional scope>): <description>

<optional body>

<optional footer>
```

- **Conventional Commits** types: `feat`, `fix`, `docs`, `style`, `refactor`, `perf`,
  `test`, `build`, `ci`, `chore`, `revert`. Use a scope when it adds clarity, e.g.
  `feat(gates):`.
- **Description**: imperative mood, lowercase, no trailing period, ≤ ~72 chars on the
  subject line.
- **Breaking changes**: append `!` after the type/scope (`feat(api)!:`) and/or a
  `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer.
- **Body** (optional): explain _why_, wrapped at ~72 cols. Add it when the change isn't
  self-explanatory.
- Respect any repo conventions found in `git log` (e.g. an issue/ticket ID footer this
  repo uses — match it).

### Emoji per type (gitmoji-aligned)

| Type       | Emoji |                              |
| ---------- | ----- | ---------------------------- |
| `feat`     | ✨    | new feature                  |
| `fix`      | 🐛    | bug fix                      |
| `docs`     | 📝    | documentation                |
| `style`    | 🎨    | formatting / code style      |
| `refactor` | ♻️    | refactor, no behavior change |
| `perf`     | ⚡️    | performance                  |
| `test`     | ✅    | tests                        |
| `build`    | 📦    | build system / dependencies  |
| `ci`       | 👷    | CI config                    |
| `chore`    | 🔧    | tooling / config / misc      |
| `revert`   | ⏪️    | revert a change              |

Other useful ones: 🚀 deploy, 🔒️ security fix, ➕ add dependency, ➖ remove dependency,
🚚 move/rename files, 🔥 remove code/files, 🚧 work in progress.

### Examples

```
✨ feat(resolver): override blocked proposals to safest allowed route
🐛 fix(payout): cap reimbursement at the policy limit
📝 docs: add "how to run" section to README
♻️ refactor(gates): extract coverage check into pure helper
✅ test: cover exactly-$10k boundary fixture
🔧 chore: pin ruff and pyright in uv.lock
```

## Rules

- Do **not** push unless the user asks.
- Do **not** add `Co-Authored-By` or tool attribution unless the user/repo requires it.
- Commit only what the user intends — surface unexpected files (build artifacts,
  secrets, large blobs) instead of silently committing them.
- Keep each commit green: don't split such that an intermediate commit breaks the build
  when it's easy to avoid.

inherits from (see docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md).

Create Date: 2026-07-23

72	## Memory lifecycle
73	
74	Ingests propose memories in `candidate` state; you review and decide:
75	
76	    working → candidate → durable
77	                      ↘ rejected
78	    durable → archived
79	
80	`wakil memory list` (with `--state`/`--type` filters) reviews them, `promote`
81	moves them to durable, `reject` removes them from search, and `archive` keeps
82	them searchable but downranked. Invalid transitions are refused. Rather than
83	deleting, retrieval fades memories: durable ranks first, then candidate, then
84	working (fading further after 30 days), then archived — and, as a secondary
85	tiebreak *within* the same state, higher-confidence memories rank ahead of
86	lower-confidence ones. Memories used to answer a query get their
87	`last_seen_at` bumped for future ranking.
88	
89	Memory `type` includes `fact | opinion | summary | relationship | question |
90	hypothesis | decision | theme | event` — `opinion` marks a subjective value
91	judgment or interpretation, as distinct from `fact`. Lifecycle `state`
92	transitions remain entirely manual (`promote`/`reject`/`archive`); there is
93	no automatic promotion or demotion based on type or confidence — a
94	low-confidence `opinion` still starts in `candidate` like everything else
95	and stays there until you act on it.
96	
97	## Selecting a workspace
98	
99	Every command accepts a global `-w`/`--workspace` option (before the
100	subcommand) naming the workspace to operate on:
101	
102	- **omitted** — use the current directory, searching upward for a `.wakil/`
103	  workspace (so any subdirectory of the knowledge base works);
104	- **a directory** — use that path (also searched upward);
105	- **a name** — look up a workspace registered by `wakil init` in
106	  `~/.config/wakil/workspaces.yaml`, so `wakil -w kb status` works from
107	  anywhere.
108	
109	The `WAKIL_WORKSPACE` environment variable provides the same value as a
110	default, e.g. `export WAKIL_WORKSPACE=kb`.
111	
112	## Skills
113	
114	A skill is a directory containing a `SKILL.md` file (Claude-Skills-compatible
115	frontmatter: `name`, `skill_api`, optional `version`), plus any supporting
116	files it needs. wakil resolves a skill name by searching, in order,
117	`WAKIL_SKILL_PATH` (a `:`-separated list of extra roots), then
118	`<kb-root>/skills`, then `~/.config/wakil/skills`, then built-in skills — the
119	first directory found wins, and a broken override blocks fallback rather than
120	being silently skipped.
121	
122	```bash
123	uv run wakil -w kb skills list                       # effective name + source
124	uv run wakil -w kb skills which meeting-synthesis -v  # selected path, roots, shadows
125	uv run wakil -w kb skills validate                    # check every root and skill
126	```
127	
128	## Ingest
129	
130	Ingest is two explicit steps.
131	
132	**Step 1 — capture** (`wakil ingest transcript|text|article`) is deterministic
133	apart from one small model call that titles and abstracts the source (see
134	ADR 0010) — the raw file's path/filename is never model-derived. Text is
135	extracted (transcripts get light cleanup: bracketed and line-leading
136	timestamps removed, whitespace normalized — never model rewriting), deduped
137	by content hash, and written under `sources/` as a raw capture. Transcript
138	frontmatter is derived from the `source` entity schema
139	(`schema/entities/source.yaml`) — its base fields plus its `transcript`
140	origin sub-schema; known fields (title, abstract, meeting date, create date,
141	origin, url) are filled in, the rest are left as blank placeholders.
142	`--context`/`-C` accepts a few lines about the source (attendees, company,
143	purpose) and is stored on the source record for step 2.
144	
145	**Step 2 — enrichment** (`wakil enrich <source-id>`) is a fixed,
146	code-sequenced pipeline of two model calls, one preview, one confirm:
147	
148	1. **Extraction** — judgment prose from `skills/<kind>/SKILL.md` (transcript,
149	   article, or text) produces the summary, key points, candidate memories
150	   (dated events carry their own `event_date`), relationships, and a proposed
151	   KB note. The capture-time context (or a fresh `--context`) plus the
152	   opening of the source drive a search for related entity notes and prior
153	   meetings, which the model links with [[wikilinks]]. Page shape and
154	   frontmatter come structurally from the entity-schema catalog; `RESOLVER.md`
155	   guidance, when present, is included so the note follows the KB's own
156	   subject-matter routing rules.
157	2. **Entity resolution** — always invoked, never optional: for each entity
158	   the source touched, the model decides create/update/skip against the
159	   existing notes and the shipped entity schemas. Notable new entities
160	   (action `create`) become stub pages with schema-valid frontmatter and a
161	   Compiled Truth / Timeline skeleton, routed into the type's canonical
162	   directory; the decisions are shown in the preview before anything is
163	   written.
164	
165	Model output is validated against Pydantic contracts (the same JSON Schema
166	shown to the model), retried once on a validation failure, and fails visibly
167	— never silently coerced. Before apply, `validate_proposal()` checks every
168	proposed file's frontmatter against the entity schemas; a proposed `type:`
169	with no schema is a hard stop, not a best-guess write. Re-running requires
170	`--force`.
171	
172	Both steps preview before writing (`--yes` skips the prompt) and accept
173	`--branch`/`--commit`/`--pr`; captures commit as `wakil source:`, enrichment
174	as `wakil ingest:`. Proposed notes fall back to `drafts/` when routing is
175	unclear or the path collides; existing files are never overwritten. Extracted
176	memories are stored as `candidate` state for review with `wakil memory`.
177	
178	`wakil sources backfill-abstract` retroactively adds a title/abstract to
179	sources captured before this feature existed — metadata-only, it never
180	re-runs enrichment.
181	
182	## Git-native changes
183	
184	When the knowledge base is a git repository, ingest can make its changes
185	reviewable git history:
186	
187	- `--commit`/`-c` commits the ingested files on the current branch, staging
188	  only the files wakil wrote (your other uncommitted work is untouched);
189	- `--branch`/`-b` first checks the working tree is clean, then creates a
190	  `wakil/ingest/<date>-<slug>` branch and commits there;
191	- `--pr` additionally pushes the branch and opens a pull request via the
192	  GitHub CLI (`gh`), when it is installed and an `origin` remote exists.
193	
194	Commits follow the wakil conventions (`wakil ingest: add ...`) and every
195	commit is recorded in the workspace database (`git_changes`). `wakil git
196	summary` shows the current branch, pending changes, recent commits, and
197	wakil-created branches; `wakil git history <path>` shows one file's history.
198	
199	## Search
200	
201	`wakil search` combines two engines: [QMD](https://github.com/tobi/qmd) over
202	the Markdown knowledge base when the `qmd` binary is installed (`--mode
203	search|vsearch|query` selects BM25, vector, or hybrid), and SQLite FTS5
204	indexes over note metadata, memories, and sources. QMD results take
205	precedence; FTS fills in workspace records QMD doesn't cover.
206	
207	## Query
208	
209	`wakil query` retrieves matching notes, memories, and sources, sends them to a
210	model as numbered context blocks, and prints a cited answer. Answers are
211	grounded: if the knowledge base doesn't support an answer, wakil says so.
212	Each query is recorded in the workspace database (`query_runs`).
213	
214	Configure a provider via environment variables (see `.env.example`):
215	
216	- `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` — uses Anthropic (default model `claude-opus-4-8`)
217	- `OPENAI_API_KEY` + `WAKIL_MODEL` (+ optional `WAKIL_OPENAI_BASE_URL`) — any
218	  OpenAI-compatible endpoint, including local model servers
219	- `WAKIL_MODEL` / `WAKIL_PROVIDER` — override the model or force a provider
220	
221	`wakil init` indexes every Markdown file in the workspace (title, frontmatter,
222	content hash), detects whether the directory is a git repository, checks for
223	QMD on the PATH, and records high-priority context files (`README.md`,
224	`AGENTS.md`, `RESOLVER.md`) when present.
225	
226	## Development
227	
228	```bash
229	uv run pytest             # tests
230	uv run ruff check         # lint
231	uv run pytest -m eval     # live-model skill evals (needs ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or another configured provider; skipped if none is set)

---
title: Explicit register/commitment Field on Memory, Excluded from Query Grounding by Default
status: accepted
date: 2026-07-23
audience: wakil design
---

# Explicit register/commitment Field on Memory, Excluded from Query Grounding by Default

## Context

Phase 1 (ADR 0013) modeled "hot takes" — casually-asserted, low-commitment
claims — indirectly, via low `confidence` and the (unaffected) `candidate`
lifecycle state. That phase was scoped explicitly as an interim measure:
`docs/memory-opinion-and-register.md`'s "Optional phase 2" proposed an
explicit `register: Literal["formal", "casual"]` field once phase 1 alone
proved insufficient to keep hot takes from grounding answers with the same
weight as a confidently-stated fact.

This phase adds that field, per the originating proposal's phase 2 scope:
an explicit, purpose-built axis for commitment/register, kept orthogonal to
`memory_type` (a `casual` `opinion` and a `casual` `fact` are both valid),
and orthogonal to `confidence` (register is about the setting a claim was
asserted in, not how certain the extractor is that it's accurately stated).

## Decision

- `CandidateMemoryModel` and `Memory` gain a nullable `formal|casual` field,
  migrated via `storage/migrations/versions/0005_memory_stance.py` (a real
  schema change, unlike phase 1's free-string `opinion` type addition).
- **Named `stance`, not `register`.** Pydantic's `ModelMetaclass` inherits
  from `abc.ABCMeta`, which defines a `register` classmethod (used for
  registering virtual subclasses); a Pydantic field literally named
  `register` shadows it, and Pydantic warns on every model class
  definition (`UserWarning: Field name "register" ... shadows an attribute
  in parent "BaseModel"`). Since `CandidateMemoryModel` is a `BaseModel`,
  the field is named `stance` there and, for consistency (no translation
  layer at the ORM boundary), on `Memory.stance` and the internal
  `CandidateMemory` dataclass in `ingest_service.py` too. The CLI and
  display layer keep the user-facing vocabulary as `register` (flag
  `wakil memory list --register`, table/detail column "Register") —
  mirroring the existing precedent of `--type` mapping to the Python
  identifier `memory_type` (avoiding a collision with the `type` builtin).
  See `docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md` for the underlying gotcha.
- The transcript extractor (`skills/transcript/SKILL.md`) sets
  `stance="casual"` for the same class of claims that already get low
  `confidence` under phase 1 guidance — the two signals are set together,
  not as alternatives.
- `wakil query` excludes `stance="casual"` memories from the answer's
  grounding context by default (`_load_text` in `app/query_service.py`
  returns `None` for them unless `include_casual=True`), via a new
  `--include-casual` CLI flag. This is exclusion, not a ranking weight —
  simpler than blending a third signal into `retrieval_rank()`'s numeric
  tiebreak, and matches the proposal's "downranks/excludes ... unless
  explicitly asked" phrasing with the simpler of the two options.
  `wakil search` is untouched: hot takes still surface there, since search
  is about finding things (including hot takes) rather than grounding a
  synthesized answer.
- `wakil memory list --register formal|casual` and the `Register` column in
  `wakil memory show`/`list` mirror the existing `--type`/`Type` filter and
  display pattern, for the same human-review reasons ADR 0013 already
  established for `opinion`.

## Consequences

- One real migration (`0005`), unlike phase 1's free-string addition —
  justified per the original proposal's own criterion ("only if phase 1
  proves insufficient"), since confidence-as-tiebreak alone still let a
  hot take ground a query answer, just ranked slightly behind a confident
  fact rather than excluded from it.
- `stance`/`register` naming asymmetry (Python/DB identifier vs. CLI/display
  vocabulary) is a deliberate, precedented choice, not an oversight — see
  the `--type`/`memory_type` precedent above.
- `search` and `query` now diverge in what they surface for the same stored
  data (search still shows casual hot takes; query's default answer
  grounding does not) — an intentional, minimal behavior split rather than
  a new ranking dimension threaded through both.

## Sources

- `docs/adr/0013-opinion-memory-type-and-confidence-ranking.md` (phase 1)
- `docs/memory-opinion-and-register.md` (originating, non-authoritative
  proposal, "Optional phase 2")
- `src/wakil/llm/schemas.py` (`CandidateMemoryModel.stance`)
- `src/wakil/app/query_service.py` (`_load_text`, `run_query`)
- `src/wakil/storage/migrations/versions/0005_memory_stance.py`

After the two fixes above got `wakil enrich` writing again, the diff preview for `companies/mosaic-private-markets.md` showed its entire `## Compiled Truth` section — a long, carefully synthesized paragraph-and-bullet block — replaced by nothing, so the file went straight from the H1 to `## Timeline / Log`. Cause: the model returned `has_update=True` (a new Timeline entry was warranted) with an empty/absent `compiled_truth` (nothing about the State needed re-synthesis) — a legitimate combination — but `_merge_entity_note` read "no compiled_truth" as "the top section is now empty" rather than "no change to the top section," and wrote exactly that. This is the precise "clobbering bug" `note-revision/SKILL.md` warns about (full-file-style regeneration silently dropping prior content), except living in wakil's own merge code rather than in model behavior — a diff-preview review would have caught it (per that skill's "diff your draft, stop if it's shorter" step), but it's better to not produce the bad diff in the first place.

Fixed by falling back to the existing top section (stripping its own trailing `---` divider) whenever `compiled_truth` is empty, instead of dropping it. If a future entity-update diff shows content vanishing rather than being added to, check whether the responsible field was actually empty in the model's response before assuming the prompt is at fault.

### CI-only test failures after a command starts requiring a model provider (a local API key masks the gap)

**Date:** 2026-07-21 · **Source:** PR #24, `feat/capture-time-title-abstract` — `test_qmd_cli.py`

`docs/adr/0010` made `wakil ingest` require a resolved `ModelClient` (capture now generates title/abstract). Two pre-existing tests in `tests/integration/test_qmd_cli.py` invoke `wakil ingest transcript` without mocking `wakil.llm.client.resolve_client`. They passed in the PR author's own environment — and were self-reported as "pytest clean" — because a real `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` happened to be set there, so `resolve_client()` silently succeeded against the live API. CI has no such key, so both failed there with "Ingest needs a model provider," exit code 1.

If a command starts requiring a model provider for the first time, grep the whole test suite for CLI invocations of that command (`runner.invoke(app, [..., "ingest"/"enrich", ...])`) — not just the test file for the change being made — since any of them can be silently relying on a real key rather than a mock. Don't trust a "pytest clean" self-report (agent or human) that wasn't run with API-key env vars explicitly unset; `env -u ANTHROPIC_API_KEY -u OPENAI_API_KEY uv run pytest -q` is the way to actually reproduce CI's clean-environment behavior locally.

### A `git commit` after manual conflict-resolution edits can silently omit the last fix (passes locally, fails in CI)

**Date:** 2026-07-22 · **Source:** PR #24, `feat/capture-time-title-abstract` — merge-conflict resolution with `main`

After resolving a merge conflict by hand and fixing two resulting test failures with further edits, `git status` showed `MM tests/unit/test_ingest_service.py` (staged *and* unstaged changes to the same file) immediately before running `git commit -m "..."` — a signal that got missed. Plain `git commit` (no `-a`, no prior `git add`) only commits the staged half; the unstaged edits — the actual fix for both failures — never made it into the commit. `pytest` run locally right after still passed, because it reads the working tree on disk, not what's actually in the commit, so the gap was invisible until CI (which checks out the real commit) failed with the exact same two pre-fix errors.

After any manual multi-file edit immediately followed by `git commit`, check `git status` for a lingering `M` in the *unstaged* column on a file just edited — `MM` (or a bare unstaged `M` right after an edit) means `git add` didn't pick up the latest change. `git commit -a` (for tracked files) or an explicit `git add <file>` right before `git commit` removes the ambiguity. More generally: a local "tests pass" result is a claim about the working tree, not about the commit that was just made — if something depends on the commit specifically (CI, a fresh clone, a teammate's pull), diff `HEAD` against the working tree (`git diff HEAD -- <file>`) before trusting that the commit is complete.

### Resolving a PR's merge conflict in the wrong worktree (similarly-named branch, no real connection to the PR)

**Date:** 2026-07-22 · **Source:** PR #25 (`fix/eval-suite-flakiness-and-skill-gaps`) merge-conflict resolution, during a multi-PR merge session with several parallel worktrees

While merging six PRs in sequence, PR #25's conflict-resolution work was done inside `.claude/worktrees/wf_7ab073ba-4f1-2` — which was actually checked out to `refactor/candidate-notes-stopword-filtering`, a *different*, already-merged-and-closed PR's branch (PR #21), reused from earlier in the session. The mistake wasn't caught until after committing and pushing, because the resolution itself was plausible-looking (real conflict markers, real code, tests passed) — only `git log --oneline` afterward revealed the branch tip didn't match. The push landed on a dead branch with no attached open PR, so it was inert (no real harm), but the actual conflict on PR #25's real branch (`fix/eval-suite-flakiness-and-skill-gaps`, which had no dedicated worktree — its commits were made directly in the main checkout) still needed to be redone from scratch in the right place.

Root cause: `git worktree list`'s auto-generated directory names (`wf_<hash>-N`) don't encode which PR/branch they hold in an obviously-checkable way at a glance, and not every branch in a multi-branch session has a 1:1 worktree — some get created directly in the main checkout instead. Before resolving a specific PR's conflict in a given worktree (or the main checkout), confirm the location's actual branch matches that PR's `headRefName` — `git branch --show-current` in the target directory, cross-checked against `gh pr view <n> --json headRefName` — rather than assuming by directory-naming convention or "the one I used last for something related."

### A Pydantic field literally named `register` silently shadows `ABCMeta.register`

**Date:** 2026-07-23 · **Source:** PR (phase 2 of `docs/adr/0014-memory-register-field-and-query-exclusion.md`), adding `CandidateMemoryModel.register`

Adding `register: Literal["formal", "casual"] | None = Field(...)` to a Pydantic `BaseModel` subclass produced `UserWarning: Field name "register" in "CandidateMemoryModel" shadows an attribute in parent "BaseModel"` on every import, plus a broken `INSERT` once the same name was mirrored onto the SQLAlchemy `Memory` model mid-refactor. Cause: Pydantic's `ModelMetaclass` inherits from `abc.ABCMeta`, which defines a `register` classmethod (for registering virtual subclasses) — a field named `register` shadows it at the class level. Instances still work correctly (`model.register` reads the field, not the classmethod), so this is easy to miss in a quick manual check; only the warning (or a linter treating warnings as errors) surfaces it.

If a Pydantic model needs a field for a "register"/"category"/"kind of speech" concept, don't use that literal name — this codebase uses `stance` instead (kept consistent on the paired SQLAlchemy column and dataclass too, to avoid a translation layer at the ORM boundary), with `register` reserved for user-facing vocabulary only (CLI flag `--register`, display column), mirroring the existing `--type` → `memory_type` precedent (`type` collides with Python's builtin the same way). Before naming any new Pydantic field, a quick sanity check — define a throwaway `class T(BaseModel): <name>: str | None = None` and watch for a `UserWarning` — catches this class of collision (also applies to `copy`, `dict`, `json`, `schema`, and other `BaseModel`/`ABCMeta` method names) before it reaches a migration or a real model.

gh pr create --title "Add memory register/stance field + query-time exclusion (Phase 2)" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Summary

Phase 2 of the memory-taxonomy work started in #26, per the originating proposal's "Optional phase 2" (`docs/memory-opinion-and-register.md`) and this repo's own ADR 0013: adds an explicit commitment/register field now that phase 1 (confidence-as-tiebreak) alone wasn't enough to keep a hot take from grounding a `wakil query` answer with the same weight as a confident fact.

- `CandidateMemoryModel`/`Memory` gain a nullable `formal|casual` field (real migration: `storage/migrations/versions/0005_memory_stance.py`), orthogonal to `memory_type` and `confidence`.
- **Named `stance`, not `register`**: Pydantic's `ModelMetaclass` inherits from `abc.ABCMeta`, whose `register` classmethod a field literally named `register` silently shadows (a `UserWarning` on every model definition, plus real breakage once mirrored onto the SQLAlchemy model). Documented in `docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md` since it's a genuinely non-obvious, likely-to-recur gotcha. CLI/display vocabulary stays `register` (`wakil memory list --register`, `Register` column) — mirrors this repo's existing `--type` → `memory_type` precedent (dodging the `type` builtin the same way).
- `transcript/SKILL.md` sets `stance="casual"` alongside low confidence for the same hot-take claims (the two signals travel together, not as alternatives).
- `wakil query` excludes `stance="casual"` memories from the answer's grounding context by default (`--include-casual` opts back in); `wakil search` is untouched — hot takes still surface there.
- `wakil memory list --register formal|casual` + a `Register` column/line, mirroring the `--type`/`opinion` display pattern from phase 1 (ADR 0013).
- ADR 0014 records the decision, including the naming rationale above.

Commit history is 4 logical change sets: schema/migration + query CLI flag, query-time exclusion + extractor guidance, list/display filter, docs.

## Test plan

- [x] `uv run pytest -q` — 414 passed, full suite green
- [x] `uv run ruff check` — clean, no warnings (confirmed the Pydantic `UserWarning` is gone after the `stance` rename)
- [x] New unit tests: `CandidateMemoryModel` accepts `stance` values / rejects invalid ones; migration adds the `stance` column on both fresh and legacy-upgrade paths, plus a roundtrip test; `stance` flows from extraction JSON through `ingest_service` into the `Memory` row; `list_memories` filters by `stance`; `run_query` excludes casual memories by default and includes them with `include_casual=True`
- [x] Integration tests: `wakil memory list --register casual` via CLI; `wakil query --include-casual` via CLI (citations present/absent as expected)
- [x] Fixed a pre-existing test fragility surfaced by this change: `test_migration_dedupes_existing_content_hash_collisions` inserted via the full `Memory` ORM class into a DB deliberately left at an old migration revision — now uses a raw SQL insert so future column additions won't break it again
EOF
)"

1. `src/wakil/llm/schemas.py` — `CandidateMemoryModel.stance: Literal["formal", "casual"] | None`.
2. `src/wakil/storage/schema.py` — `Memory.stance: Mapped[str | None]`, migrated via `src/wakil/storage/migrations/versions/0005_memory_stance.py` (new nullable column, no default, no CHECK constraint).
3. `src/wakil/app/ingest_service.py` — internal `CandidateMemory` dataclass gains `stance`, wired through both mapping sites (extraction-output → `CandidateMemory`, and `CandidateMemory` → `Memory` ORM row).
4. `src/wakil/skills/transcript/SKILL.md` — extractor guidance: hot takes get `stance="casual"` alongside existing low-confidence guidance.
5. `src/wakil/app/query_service.py` — `_load_text`/`_build_contexts`/`run_query` gain `include_casual: bool = False`; a memory with `stance == "casual"` is excluded from the query's grounding context unless `include_casual=True`. `wakil search` is NOT touched — only `wakil query`.
6. `src/wakil/cli/main.py` — `wakil query` gains `--include-casual`; `wakil memory list` gains `--register` (CLI-facing name), which is passed internally as `list_memories(stance=register)`.

The fix was one clarifying sentence separating the link decision from the content decision — but the gap was invisible without actually running the eval. When adding or editing skill guidance, write (or extend) its `eval.json` scenario and run it live before considering the change done, not just at merge/CI time.

content.text: This detached-HEAD incident is a real, recurring-risk gotcha (a subagent checked out individual commits to test them in isolation, then never returned to the branch) — and there's direct precedent for this kind of git-workflow entry in `TROUBLESHOOTING.md` already (the "wrong worktree" entry). result.output:
185	### Resolving a PR's merge conflict in the wrong worktree (similarly-named branch, no real connection to the PR)
186	
187	**Date:** 2026-07-22 · **Source:** PR #25 (`fix/eval-suite-flakiness-and-skill-gaps`) merge-conflict resolution, during a multi-PR merge session with several parallel worktrees
188	
189	While merging six PRs in sequence, PR #25's conflict-resolution work was done inside `.claude/worktrees/wf_7ab073ba-4f1-2` — which was actually checked out to `refactor/candidate-notes-stopword-filtering`, a *different*, already-merged-and-closed PR's branch (PR #21), reused from earlier in the session. The mistake wasn't caught until after committing and pushing, because the resolution itself was plausible-looking (real conflict markers, real code, tests passed) — only `git log --oneline` afterward revealed the branch tip didn't match. The push landed on a dead branch with no attached open PR, so it was inert (no real harm), but the actual conflict on PR #25's real branch (`fix/eval-suite-flakiness-and-skill-gaps`, which had no dedicated worktree — its commits were made directly in the main checkout) still needed to be redone from scratch in the right place.
190	
191	Root cause: `git worktree list`'s auto-generated directory names (`wf_<hash>-N`) don't encode which PR/branch they hold in an obviously-checkable way at a glance, and not every branch in a multi-branch session has a 1:1 worktree — some get created directly in the main checkout instead. Before resolving a specific PR's conflict in a given worktree (or the main checkout), confirm the location's actual branch matches that PR's `headRefName` — `git branch --show-current` in the target directory, cross-checked against `gh pr view <n> --json headRefName` — rather than assuming by directory-naming convention or "the one I used last for something related."
192	
193	### A Pydantic field literally named `register` silently shadows `ABCMeta.register`
194	
195	**Date:** 2026-07-23 · **Source:** PR (phase 2 of `docs/adr/0014-memory-register-field-and-query-exclusion.md`), adding `CandidateMemoryModel.register`
196	
197	Adding `register: Literal["formal", "casual"] | None = Field(...)` to a Pydantic `BaseModel` subclass produced `UserWarning: Field name "register" in "CandidateMemoryModel" shadows an attribute in parent "BaseModel"` on every import, plus a broken `INSERT` once the same name was mirrored onto the SQLAlchemy `Memory` model mid-refactor. Cause: Pydantic's `ModelMetaclass` inherits from `abc.ABCMeta`, which defines a `register` classmethod (for registering virtual subclasses) — a field named `register` shadows it at the class level. content.text:
## Packaging `wakil` as a system-wide CLI command

`pyproject.toml` already declares `wakil = "wakil.cli.main:app"` under `[project.scripts]`, so this is just "install it," not "add entry points."

- **`uv tool install --editable .` (recommended)** — installs `wakil` onto your PATH in an isolated venv, but symlinked to this checkout, so `git pull` + no reinstall keeps it current. Best fit since you're actively developing it.
- **`uv tool install .`** — same isolation, but a frozen snapshot; re-run after every change you want reflected.
- **`pipx install -e .`** — same idea as the first option, for if you'd rather not depend on `uv`'s tool manager specifically.
- **Shell alias/function** (`alias wakil='uv run --project ~/Projects/wakil wakil'`) — zero install step, always runs from source, but slower per-invocation (dependency resolution check) and ties the alias to this exact path.

## Hermes access to meeting/article ingest

Wakil's ingest is already a stable two-step CLI (`wakil ingest transcript|article`, `wakil enrich <id>`), and its own design bias is explicit CLI commands over multi-agent orchestration — so:

- **Shell out from a Hermes skill (recommended)** — a Hermes skill/tool definition invokes the installed `wakil` CLI as a subprocess (`wakil ingest transcript ... --context ... --pr`). No new code in wakil; just requires it installed per above and a short Hermes-side skill doc describing when/how to call it.
- **MCP server wrapping wakil** — build a small MCP server exposing `ingest`/`enrich` as tools, so Hermes calls them natively instead of shelling out. More native, but real new code/surface to maintain — only worth it if Hermes needs structured tool-call results rather than parsed CLI output.
- **Direct Python import** (Hermes imports `wakil.app.ingest_service` directly) — tightest coupling, skips the CLI boundary entirely; couples Hermes to wakil's internal API rather than its intended-stable CLI surface. I'd avoid this.

My lean: CLI-install + shell-out-from-a-skill covers this with no new wakil code at all; reach for the MCP server only if Hermes specifically needs structured (not text) results back.

# Ed's Narrative Voice

Write narrative documents the way Ed writes them: lean, concrete, and emotionally
restrained. The prose should feel simple and elegant on the surface even when the
underlying situation is complicated. The reader should never notice the writing —
only the substance.

This skill is for standalone prose: documentation, READMEs, essays, design docs,
retrospectives, blog posts, debriefs, write-ups. For emails, defer to the
`email-voice` skill.

## The voice in one paragraph

Ed leads with the point, states facts plainly, and lets precise details carry the
weight that other writers hand to adjectives. Sentences are short and declarative.
Claims come with evidence — a number, a date, a named system, a concrete example.
Tension and trade-offs are named directly, costs included, without drama or
apology. He trusts the reader: no over-explaining motives, no belaboring subtext,
no telling the reader how to feel.

## Principles

**Lead with the point.** The first sentence of a document — and of each section —
carries the conclusion. Context follows; it never precedes. "Just wrapped with
Khalil — a really positive call, and I'm more interested after it than before."
Everything after that sentence is support.

**Concrete over abstract.** Prefer the named thing to the category: not "improved
performance significantly" but "the application got ~80% faster"; not "a complex
data problem" but "transforming messy documents into trustworthy structured data."
If a claim has a number, a date, or a proper noun available, use it.

**Emotional restraint.** State the fact and stop. The situation's weight comes
from the facts, not from the narration. Never editorialize ("remarkably",
"impressively", "unfortunately"), never dramatize stakes, never perform enthusiasm
or dismay in prose. If something matters, the details will show it.

**Name tensions plainly.** When there's a conflict, cost, or caveat, say it in one
flat sentence and give the reasoning: "One thing I want to be transparent about:
I'm ideally looking for a role that's more hands-on, and this one leans more
heavily toward leadership." State the cost of a decision honestly, then why it was
right anyway. Never bury a trade-off and never apologize for one.

**Don't over-explain motives.** Give the reason once, in one clause, and move on.
The reader can infer the rest. Three sentences justifying a choice is two too
many.

**Plain words.** Short Anglo-Saxon words over Latinate ones where they fit: "use"
not "utilize", "build" not "architect" (as a verb), "so" not "consequently". No
jargon unless it's the domain's real vocabulary.

## Sentence-level habits

- Short declarative sentences as the default. Vary length occasionally so the
  rhythm doesn't go mechanical, but when in doubt, cut the sentence in two.
- Em-dashes for compression — an appositive or pivot mid-sentence rather than a
  new subordinate clause.
- Contrast constructions to sharpen a claim: "That's the founding-CTO shape, not
  a pure people-management cleanup role." "Speed is negotiable; a divergent study
  result is not."
- Contractions are fine. This is professional prose, not formal prose.

Here's the planned outline for `~/Projects/kb/skills/wakil-ingest/SKILL.md`, matching `narrative-voice`'s frontmatter convention (`name`/`description`/`skill_api: 1`):

2. **Scope statement** — shells out to the real `wakil` CLI only; never reimplements ingest logic or hand-writes notes into the kb directly. Doesn't cover producing the raw transcript/article text itself (that's upstream), and doesn't cover memory review/promotion (that stays a separate, human-driven step via `wakil memory list`).

5. **Enrich step** — `wakil enrich <source-id>`, same context flags, `--force` for re-runs.
6. **Confirmation/autonomy policy** — when to pass `--yes` vs. show the preview and stop (pending decision below); never use `--force` casually.
7. **Git-flow awareness** — default branches+commits+opens a draft PR; when `--local` is appropriate instead.
8. **Error handling** — no provider configured, "already ingested" duplicate, unresolvable workspace.
9. **"Don't guess" instruction** — if a command doesn't behave as documented, run `wakil ingest --help` / `wakil enrich --help` rather than inventing flags, since this doc can drift from the real CLI.

---
name: wakil-ingest
description: "Capture and enrich a meeting transcript or web article into Ed's wakil knowledge base by shelling out to the `wakil` CLI. Use this whenever Ed asks to ingest, capture, log, or add a meeting/call/transcript or an article/link to his knowledge base — even if he just says something like 'add this to the kb' or 'log this call'. Not for writing notes by hand, not for searching/querying the kb (a separate skill), and not for reviewing/promoting memories afterward (Ed does that himself with `wakil memory`)."
skill_api: 1
---

# wakil ingest

Shell out to the real `wakil` CLI to capture and enrich sources into Ed's
knowledge base at `~/Projects/kb`. This skill never reimplements ingest logic,
never hand-writes notes directly into the kb, and never guesses at a `wakil`
flag it hasn't verified.

## Scope

- **In scope**: capturing a meeting/call transcript or a web article, then
  running enrichment so it becomes searchable memories and (usually) a linked
  note.
- **Out of scope**: producing the raw transcript/article text itself (that
  already exists as a file or URL before this skill starts); reviewing or
  promoting the resulting memories (`wakil memory list|promote|reject|archive`
  stays a separate, later, human-driven step); search/query over the kb (use
  `wakil search`/`wakil query` directly, or a dedicated query skill).

## Prerequisites

- `wakil` is on `PATH` (`uv tool install --editable` from `~/Projects/wakil`).
- A model provider is configured: `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, or `OPENAI_API_KEY` +
  `WAKIL_MODEL` for an OpenAI-compatible endpoint.
- The workspace is addressed as `-w kb` (registered name — resolves to
  `~/Projects/kb`). If `-w kb` ever reports the wrong root or a stale
  database, the registry is corrupt; fix it with
  `wakil init ~/Projects/kb --name kb` (safe to re-run — it only re-registers
  and re-indexes, never destroys existing data) before ingesting anything.

## Design note: auto-confirm, not auto-merge

Every command below passes `--yes` — no interactive confirmation prompt, by
deliberate choice, so this skill can run unattended. This is a real departure
from `wakil`'s own default (preview-then-confirm) design bias, so the
mitigation is load-bearing and must not be dropped: **never pass `--local`**,
so every capture/enrich still branches, commits, and opens (or updates) a
*draft* PR rather than writing straight to `main`. The draft PR is the review
point — Ed reviews and merges it himself, later. Never merge the PR as part
of this skill; that is always a separate, explicit, human action.

## Step 1 — capture

```bash
wakil -w kb ingest transcript <path-to-transcript> \
  --context "<attendees, company/counterparty, purpose>" \
  --yes
```

```bash
wakil -w kb ingest article <url> \
  --context "<why this was captured, if not obvious>" \
  --yes
```

`--context`/`-C` is repeatable; use `--context-file <path>` to attach a prep
note or agenda instead of (or alongside) inline text — it supports
`@file:PATH` / `@url:URL` expansion on its own, so don't manually paste a
whole file's contents into `--context` if `--context-file` can take it
directly.

Read the command's own output for the new **source id** (`Sources` count /
capture result) — the next step needs it. If the output instead says
"Already ingested (matches source #N)", nothing new was written; treat `N`
as the source id and skip straight to enrichment (it may not be enriched yet
even if the raw capture already existed).

## Step 2 — enrich

```bash
wakil -w kb enrich <source-id> --yes
```

Same `--context`/`--context-file` options apply here too, independently of
whatever was passed at capture time — use them if there's context relevant
to *analysis* (e.g. clarifying an ambiguous name) that wasn't needed for the
raw capture. Add `--force` only if explicitly asked to re-analyze a source
that was already enriched — never use it reflexively to "make an error go
away."

## Error handling

- **"Ingest needs a model provider" / "Enrichment needs a model provider"**
  — a provider env var is missing; report this plainly rather than retrying.
- **"Already ingested (matches source #N)"** — not an error; see Step 1.
- **Workspace resolution failure** — if `-w kb` fails to resolve at all,
  don't fall back to guessing a path; report it and suggest re-running
  `wakil init ~/Projects/kb --name kb`.
- **Any other non-zero exit** — report the command and its full output
  verbatim; don't retry blindly or silently add flags to work around it.

## If a command doesn't behave as documented here

This file can drift from the real CLI. Run `wakil ingest --help`,
`wakil ingest transcript --help`, or `wakil enrich --help` to check the
actual current flags before improvising one that isn't written above.

## Worked examples

**A call transcript, already saved as a file:**
```bash
wakil -w kb ingest transcript ~/Downloads/2026-07-23-pedro-call.txt \
  --context "Pedro Franceschi, Brex CEO, quarterly catch-up" \
  --yes
# -> "source #87"
wakil -w kb enrich 87 --yes
```

**A web article:**
```bash
wakil -w kb ingest article https://example.com/some-article --yes
# -> "source #88"
wakil -w kb enrich 88 --yes
```

# quickcapture-ingest (Claude Code wrapper)

Thin wrapper over the Hermes skill. **Read and follow the full procedure in
`.hermes/skills/quickcapture-ingest/SKILL.md`**.

`sources/captured-notes.md` is an **inbox**: notes are appended by the
[QuickCapture iOS app](https://quickcaptureobsidian.app/). Each entry is a
`<note captured="{yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss}" status="{not-ingested|ingested}">…</note>`
element terminated by a `---`. The skill consumes entries whose
`status="not-ingested"` one at a time, files each to its canonical home, marks it
`status="ingested"` in place (never deleting it — this avoids merge conflicts on
the shared inbox), and commits.

## What it does (see the Hermes SKILL for the full phases)

1. **Parse** `sources/captured-notes.md` — each entry is a `<note captured="…"
   status="…">…</note>` element ending at `---`. Process only `status="not-ingested"`
   notes; skip `ingested` ones. Attribute quotes may be straight or curly — parse
   both. Normalize the `captured` timestamp to ISO; QuickCapture sometimes emits
   invalid dates — validate and flag.
2. **Classify** each entry — first match wins: tweet/X → web URL → image →
   voice note → typed idea (file by primary subject, not format).
3. **Route** via the vault `RESOLVER.md` and shape per `schema.md`, delegating to
   the matching skill (`media-ingest`, `article-enrichment`, `voice-note-ingest`,
   `idea-ingest`, `enrich`). **Tweets are two-stage:** land the verbatim tweet as a
   raw `sources/tweets/<slug>.md` source note first, then enrich its content into
   the brain (concept / person / company / media) with links both ways. X can't be
   read by WebFetch (402) — pull tweet text via the logged-in Chrome session.
4. **Preserve provenance** with an inline `[Source: ...]` citation carrying the
   capture timestamp and origin URL.
5. **Cross-link** every mentioned person/company (Iron Law); update existing
   pages surgically — never clobber.
6. **Mark ingested (never delete)** — flip each routed note's `status` from
   `not-ingested` to `ingested` in place; leave un-routable ones as
   `not-ingested` and flag them.
7. **Commit** per `.hermes/skills/knowledge-base/kb-commit/SKILL.md`.

## gbrain tools — MCP first (see CLAUDE.md § gbrain MCP server)

If the `gbrain` MCP server is connected, **use the `mcp__gbrain__*` tools**
(`search`, `get_page`, `put_page`, `add_link`, `add_timeline_entry`,
`get_backlinks`). If it is **not** connected, **warn the user and stop — do NOT
silently fall back** to file operations.

**File-operation fallback** — only after the user explicitly opts into file-only mode:

| gbrain tool | File-only fallback |
|-------------|--------------------|
| `search` / `get_page` | `Grep` / `Glob` / `Read` the vault |
| `put_page` | `Write` / `Edit` the page (follow `schema.md`) |
| `add_link` | edit `[[wikilinks]]` + back-links |
| `add_timeline_entry` | append a dated entry to the page's Timeline |

Honor `RESOLVER.md` placement, `schema.md` frontmatter, and the citation +
back-link rules in `.hermes/skills/conventions/quality.md`. The skill does **not**
push — remind the user to `git push` per the session-close protocol.

6	
7	# wakil KB Administration
8	
9	wakil (`~/Projects/wakil`) is an actively-developed local-first CLI agent for
10	markdown knowledge bases. It changes fast — its own architecture docs
11	(README, PROMPT.md) can already be stale relative to accepted ADRs. Two hard
12	rules before doing anything else in this space:
13	
14	## Rule 1: verify wakil's current architecture against its own source, not memory or README prose
15	
16	Before advising on RESOLVER.md/SCHEMA.md conventions, entity types, or
17	workspace mechanics, actually read:
18	
19	- `src/wakil/schema/entities/*.yaml` — the real, current entity catalog
20	- `src/wakil/schema/loader.py` — resolution precedence (its own module
21	  docstring states the mirrored-from-skills precedence explicitly)
22	- `docs/adr/*.md` — accepted architecture decisions; a `status: accepted`
23	  ADR overrides anything README/PROMPT.md still says
24	- `docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md` — known gotchas, dated, with root causes
25	
26	**Concretely, as of ADR 0011 (accepted 2026-07-21): `SCHEMA.md` is retired as
27	a code dependency.** Frontmatter shape no longer comes from a hand-authored
28	prose file — it comes from the code-owned entity-schema catalog
29	(`schema/entities/*.yaml`), one file per `type`, resolved **kb-local →
30	user (`~/.config/wakil/schema/entities/`) → built-in**, first-match-wins,
31	whole-file, no merging — the same precedence pattern skill resolution
32	already uses (ADR 0001). `RESOLVER.md` survives but its job narrowed: entity
33	routing is now code-owned via each schema's `directory:` field (not a
34	judgment call); `RESOLVER.md` is authority only for what a static per-type
35	schema can't express — subject-matter subdirectory routing for non-entity
36	content, sensitivity overrides that cut across types, naming/linking
37	conventions, and concept-vs-project-style ambiguity judgment. See
38	`references/wakil-architecture-notes.md` for the fuller ADR digest
39	(ADR 0011, ADR 0012 proposed-built-in-RESOLVER.md-default) before assuming
40	either file's old (pre-2026-07) behavior.
41	
42	If asked to scaffold a workspace, don't write a prose SCHEMA.md at all —
43	author `schema/entities/<type>.yaml` files instead (see below).
44	
45	## Rule 2: don't assert a tool/plugin limitation without checking
46	
47	Corrected once in this class of work: claimed Obsidian vaults structurally
48	cannot link to each other. Wrong — the built-in `obsidian://vault/<vault>/
49	<note>` URI scheme and the Advanced URI community plugin (stable-UUID-based
50	links that survive renames) both do this natively. Actively-maintained
51	ecosystems (Obsidian, wakil, any plugin-based tool) gain capability
52	continuously; a quick search beats a confident negative claim, especially
53	one that would materially change the design being proposed. Confirm before
54	telling a user something "isn't possible."
55	
56	## Entity schema authoring
57	
58	Each file in `schema/entities/` declares one type:
59	
60	```yaml
61	type: <type-name>
62	directory: <canonical-directory>      # code-owned destination, not RESOLVER.md's job
63	category: identity | document | hybrid  # governs name:/title: — enforced as a hard error, not style
64	page_shape: compiled-truth-timeline | single-occurrence
65	fields:
66	  <field-name>: {required: bool, kind: string|list|ref|enum|date|bool|int, values: [...] (enum only), ref_type: <type> (ref only)}
67	```
68	
69	- **`category` rule is enforced in code** (`schema/validate.py`): `identity`
70	  types forbid `title:`, `document` types forbid `name:`, `identity`/`hybrid`
71	  types require `name:`. Get this wrong and validation hard-fails, not warns.
72	- **`page_shape` is a separate axis from `category`** — don't infer one from
73	  the other. `compiled-truth-timeline` = accumulates knowledge across many
74	  sources over time (Compiled Truth + append-only Timeline). `single-
75	  occurrence` = one dated event/artifact, no Timeline.
76	- **Extending a built-in type** (e.g. adding enum values to `person`'s
77	  `relationship` field): copy the built-in file's shape into
78	  `<kb-root>/schema/entities/<type>.yaml` and edit — kb-local wins whole-file
79	  over built-in, no merging, so the override must be complete, not a diff.
80	- **`kind: ref` is not currently validated against real entities** — it only
81	  checks the value is a string. A cross-vault or cross-repo pointer string in
82	  a `ref` field will validate fine; don't expect wakil to catch a broken
83	  reference.
84	- Run `wakil -w <name> schema list` to see the effective catalog (confirms
85	  kb-local overrides actually resolve) and `wakil -w <name> schema which
86	  <type>` to see which root won for one type. There is no `schema validate`
87	  subcommand (only `list`/`which`/`migrate`) — don't invent one.
88	- **Verification pattern**: write a throwaway ad-hoc Python script (not part
89	  of any test suite, delete after) that imports `wakil.schema.loader` /
90	  `wakil.schema.validate` directly and exercises: (a) the catalog loads
91	  without `SchemaLoadError`, (b) new types resolve from the expected root,
92	  (c) representative valid frontmatter for each new/changed type passes
93	  `validate_frontmatter`, (d) representative invalid frontmatter (bad enum,
94	  missing required field, wrong category field) is correctly *rejected* —
95	  a schema that never rejects anything is as broken as one that rejects
96	  everything. See `scripts/verify-schema-catalog.py` for a template.
97	
98	## Workspace registration — mechanics and a real gotcha
99	
100	`~/.config/wakil/workspaces.yaml` is a **pure client-side alias**, `name →
101	root_path`, written by `wakil init <path> --name <name>`. It carries no
102	other state; each workspace is fully self-contained in its own `.wakil/`
103	(config.yaml + wakil.db, already gitignored). Omitting `-w` just walks
104	upward from cwd for a `.wakil/` directory — the registry is a convenience,
105	not a requirement.
106	
107	**Gotcha hit in practice**: if `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` is set in the *current
108	session's* environment (check `echo $XDG_CONFIG_HOME` — a Hermes session can
109	have this repointed at a project directory, e.g. `<kb-root>/.config`),
110	`wakil init`/registry reads and writes go to `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/wakil/`, not
111	the user's real `~/.config/wakil/` that their normal shell will resolve.
112	This fails silently — no error, just a registry entry written to the wrong
113	place, or (worse) a stale entry read from the wrong place while a real one
114	sits unused elsewhere. Before relying on `wakil init --name` or the
115	registry: check `echo $XDG_CONFIG_HOME`; if it's set to something other than
116	the user's real config home, re-run the registration with
117	`env -u XDG_CONFIG_HOME wakil init <path> --name <name>` so the *actual*
118	`~/.config/wakil/workspaces.yaml` the user's shell will use gets the entry,
119	and verify with `cat ~/.config/wakil/workspaces.yaml` (absolute path, not
120	`$XDG_CONFIG_HOME`-relative) afterward.
121	
122	## Scaffolding a new wakil-managed vault — checklist
123	
124	1. Design the directory tree and entity types first (see
125	   `references/cross-vault-linking-options.md` if this vault needs to
126	   relate to another existing vault — four real topology options with
127	   tradeoffs, not just "yes/no possible").
128	2. `mkdir -p` the tree; empty directories need a `.gitkeep` placeholder to be
129	   committed and visible on clone.
130	3. Write `RESOLVER.md` scoped to *only* the residual judgment calls a static
131	   schema can't express (see Rule 1) — don't duplicate entity routing tables
132	   that `schema.directory` already owns.
133	4. Write `schema/entities/*.yaml` for every new type, plus any kb-local
134	   overrides of built-in types.
135	5. Write `CLAUDE.md`/`AGENTS.md` pointing at RESOLVER.md and explaining the
136	   schema-catalog-not-prose-SCHEMA.md convention for future agent sessions.
137	6. `git init`, commit the scaffold.
138	7. `wakil init <path> --name <name>` (checking the XDG gotcha above first).
139	8. Verify: `wakil -w <name> schema list` (confirms overrides resolve),
140	   `wakil -w <name> git summary` (confirms clean working tree), and the
141	   ad-hoc verification script pattern above for anything non-trivial in the
142	   new schemas.
143	
144	## git-crypt / at-rest encryption for sensitive content
145	
146	No wakil code changes needed — git-crypt is a git clean/smudge filter
147	configured entirely via `.gitattributes` (`<path-glob> filter=git-crypt
148	diff=git-crypt`). wakil only does file I/O against the working tree, which
149	stays plaintext whenever the repo is unlocked, so ingest/enrich/search all
150	keep working unmodified. Two caveats to state explicitly when recommending
151	this, not silently: (1) `.wakil/wakil.db`'s local FTS/QMD index will hold a
152	plaintext derived copy of anything git-crypt encrypts — this protects git
153	history/remote, not the local machine; (2) never run wakil against a
154	`git-crypt lock`ed repo — frontmatter parsing will choke on ciphertext.
155

157

1	# Quality Convention
2	
3	Cross-cutting quality rules for all brain-writing skills.
4	
5	## Citations (MANDATORY)
6	
7	Every fact written to a brain page must carry an inline `[Source: ...]` citation.
8	
9	- **User's statements:** `[Source: User, {context}, YYYY-MM-DD]`
10	- **Meeting data:** `[Source: Meeting "{title}", YYYY-MM-DD]`
11	- **Email/message:** `[Source: email from {name} re: {subject}, YYYY-MM-DD]`
12	- **Web content:** `[Source: {publication}, {URL}, YYYY-MM-DD]`
13	- **Social media:** `[Source: X/@handle, YYYY-MM-DD](URL)`
14	- **Synthesis:** `[Source: compiled from {sources}]`
15	
16	### Source precedence (highest to lowest)
17	
18	1. User's direct statements (highest authority)
19	2. Compiled truth (brain's synthesized understanding)
20	3. Timeline entries (raw evidence)
21	4. External sources (API enrichment, web search)
22	
23	## Back-Linking (MANDATORY)
24	
25	Every mention of a person or company WITH a brain page MUST create a back-link
26	FROM that entity's page TO the page mentioning them.
27	
28	Format: `- **YYYY-MM-DD** | Referenced in [page title](path) -- context`
29	
30	An unlinked mention is a broken brain.
31	
32	## Page-Update Discipline (MANDATORY)
33	
34	A brain page is a **cumulative ledger**, not a scratchpad. Updating an existing
35	page MUST preserve what is already there. The failure this prevents: regenerating
36	a whole page from only the newest source, which silently drops prior knowledge
37	(the "Scorealytics Regression", 2026-06-11 — `companies/scorealytics.md`,
38	`people/lawrence-krubner.md`, and the mentoring-program page were each rewritten
39	from a single transcript, wiping frontmatter, distilled history, and timelines).
40	
41	Treat each region of a page by its own rule:
42	
43	- **Compiled Truth / State** — *re-synthesize*, covering the **union of existing
44	  State + new facts**. "Rewrite the State section" means *re-derive it from
45	  everything known*, NOT *replace it with the latest source*. Losing a
46	  previously-synthesized fact is a regression, not an update.
47	- **Timeline / Log** — *append-only*. Add new dated entries; never delete, rewrite,
48	  or reorder existing ones. The auto-generated back-link lines are part of the
49	  Timeline — preserve them too.
50	- **YAML frontmatter** — *preserve*. Add or update values, but never strip the block
51	  or drop schema-required keys (see `schema.md`). A removed key breaks GBrain entity
52	  detection. Delete a key only to fix a genuinely malformed field.
53	- **H1 heading** — *equals the kebab-case filename slug* (`# lawrence-krubner`, not
54	  `# Lawrence Krubner`). Never retitle it to Title Case or a "summary" heading.
55	
56	**Method:** prefer surgical edits (append a Timeline entry; edit the State block)
57	over full-file rewrites of an existing page — full regeneration is the *mechanism*
58	that enables clobbering. Before saving, diff your output against the current page:
59	**if your version is shorter, assume you are clobbering and stop.**
60	
61	**Mechanical backstop:** `.githooks/pre-commit` blocks any commit that shrinks a
62	guarded entity page by >40% or drops YAML keys. For an intentional
63	prune/archive/merge/split, override with `ALLOW_ENTITY_SHRINK=1 git commit …`.
64	
65	## Notability Gate
66	
67	Before creating a new brain page, check notability:
68	
69	- **People:** Will you interact again? Relevant to work/interests?
70	- **Companies:** Relevant to work/job-search/interests?
71	- **Concepts:** Reusable mental model? Worth referencing again?
72	
73	When in doubt, DON'T create. A 400-follower person who tweeted once is not notable.

1	# Brain Filing Rules -- MANDATORY for all skills that write to the brain
2	
3	## The Rule
4	
5	The PRIMARY SUBJECT of the content determines where it goes. Not the format,
6	not the source, not the skill that's running.
7	
8	## Decision Protocol
9	
10	1. Identify the primary subject (a person? company? concept? policy issue?)
11	2. File in the directory that matches the subject
12	3. Cross-link from related directories
13	4. When in doubt: what would you search for to find this page again?
14	
15	## Common Misfiling Patterns -- DO NOT DO THESE
16	
17	| Wrong | Right | Why |
18	|-------|-------|-----|
19	| Analysis of a topic -> `sources/` | -> appropriate subject directory | sources/ is for raw data only |
20	| Article about a person -> `sources/` | -> `people/` | Primary subject is a person |
21	| Meeting-derived company info -> `meetings/` only | -> ALSO update `companies/` | Entity propagation is mandatory |
22	| Research about a company -> `sources/` | -> `companies/` | Primary subject is a company |
23	| Reusable framework/thesis -> `sources/` | -> `concepts/` | It's a mental model |
24	| Tweet thread about policy -> `media/` | -> `civic/` or `concepts/` | media/ is for content ops |
25	
26	## Sanctioned exception: synthesis output is _sui generis_
27	
28	The "file by primary subject" rule is for raw ingest. Synthesized output that
29	is one-of-one to a single source AND a specific reader (a personalized book
30	mirror, a strategic-reading playbook tied to one problem) does not fit any
31	subject directory cleanly: filing by topic loses the "this is the book"
32	dimension; filing by author muddles authorship pages with synthesis pages.
33	
34	Format-prefixed paths under `media/<format>/<slug>` are the sanctioned
35	exception:
36	
37	- `media/books/<slug>-personalized.md` (book-mirror output)
38	- `media/articles/<slug>-personalized.md` (long-form article personalization)
39	
40	If you find yourself wanting `media/<format>/` for raw ingest, that is still
41	the anti-pattern in the table above. The exception is narrow: synthesized,
42	one-of-one, _sui generis_ to a single source.
43	
44	## What `sources/` Is Actually For
45	
46	`sources/` is ONLY for:
47	- Bulk data imports (API dumps, CSV exports, snapshots)
48	- Raw data that feeds multiple brain pages (e.g., a guest export, contact sync)
49	- Periodic captures (quarterly snapshots, sync exports)
50	
51	If the content has a clear primary subject (a person, company, concept, policy
52	issue), it does NOT go in sources/. Period.
53	
54	## Notability Gate
55	
56	Not everything deserves a brain page. Before creating a new entity page:
57	- **People:** Will you interact with them again? Are they relevant to your work?
58	- **Companies:** Are they relevant to your work or interests?
59	- **Concepts:** Is this a reusable mental model worth referencing later?
60	- **When in doubt, DON'T create.** A missing page can be created later.
61	  A junk page wastes attention and degrades search quality.
62	
63	## Iron Law: Back-Linking (MANDATORY)
64	
65	Every mention of a person or company with a brain page MUST create a back-link
66	FROM that entity's page TO the page mentioning them. This is bidirectional:
67	the new page links to the entity, AND the entity's page links back.
68	
69	Format for back-links (append to Timeline or See Also):
70	```
71	- **YYYY-MM-DD** | Referenced in [page title](path/to/page.md) -- brief context
72	```
73	
74	An unlinked mention is a broken brain. The graph is the intelligence.
75	
76	## Citation Requirements (MANDATORY)
77	
78	Every fact written to a brain page must carry an inline `[Source: ...]` citation.
79	
80	Three formats:
81	- **Direct attribution:** `[Source: User, {context}, YYYY-MM-DD]`
82	- **API/external:** `[Source: {provider}, YYYY-MM-DD]` or `[Source: {publication}, {URL}]`
83	- **Synthesis:** `[Source: compiled from {list of sources}]`
84	
85	Source precedence (highest to lowest):
86	1. User's direct statements (highest authority)
87	2. Compiled truth (pre-existing brain synthesis)
88	3. Timeline entries (raw evidence)
89	4. External sources (API enrichment, web search -- lowest)
90	
91	When sources conflict, note the contradiction with both citations. Don't
92	silently pick one.
93	
94	## Raw Source Preservation
95	
96	Every ingested item should have its raw source preserved for provenance.
97	
98	**Size routing (automatic via `gbrain files upload-raw`):**
99	- **< 100 MB text/PDF**: stays in the brain repo (git-tracked) in a `.raw/`
100	  sidecar directory alongside the brain page
101	- **>= 100 MB OR media files** (video, audio, images): uploaded to cloud
102	  storage (Supabase Storage, S3, etc.) with a `.redirect.yaml` pointer left
103	  in the brain repo. Files >= 100 MB use TUS resumable upload (6 MB chunks
104	  with retry) for reliability.
105	
106	**Upload command:**
107	```bash
108	gbrain files upload-raw <file> --page <page-slug> --type <type>
109	```
110	Returns JSON: `{storage: "git"}` for small files, `{storage: "supabase", storagePath, reference}` for cloud.
111	
112	**The `.redirect.yaml` pointer format:**
113	```yaml
114	target: supabase://brain-files/page-slug/filename.mp4
115	bucket: brain-files
116	storage_path: page-slug/filename.mp4
117	size: 524288000
118	size_human: 500 MB
119	hash: sha256:abc123...
120	mime: video/mp4
121	uploaded: 2026-04-11T...
122	type: transcript
123	```
124	
125	**Accessing stored files:**
126	```bash
127	gbrain files signed-url <storage-path>    # Generate 1-hour signed URL
128	gbrain files restore <dir>                # Download back to local
129	```
130	
131	This ensures any derived brain page can be traced back to its original source,
132	and large files don't bloat the git repo.
133	
134	## Dream-cycle synthesize / patterns directories (v0.23)
135	
136	The `synthesize` and `patterns` phases of `gbrain dream` write to a
137	**fixed allow-list** of paths sourced from `_brain-filing-rules.json`'s
138	`dream_synthesize_paths.globs` array. Editing that JSON is the ONLY way
139	to add a new directory the synthesis subagent may write to:
140	
141	| Output type | Slug pattern | What goes here |
142	|-------------|--------------|----------------|
143	| Reflection | `wiki/personal/reflections/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>-<hash[:6]>` | Self-knowledge, emotional processing, pattern recognition. Verbatim quotes from the user, with analysis. |
144	| Original idea | `wiki/originals/ideas/YYYY-MM-DD-<idea>-<hash[:6]>` | New frames, theses, mental models, "conceptive ideologist" outputs. Capture the user's exact phrasing — that's the artifact. |
145	| People enrichment | `wiki/people/<existing-slug>` | Timeline entries appended to existing people pages from session mentions. Stub pages for new substantive people. |
146	| Pattern | `wiki/personal/patterns/<theme>` | Cross-session theme detected across ≥3 reflections. Highest-leverage output: a pattern can span 25 years if reflections reference dated content. |
147	| Cycle summary | `dream-cycle-summaries/YYYY-MM-DD` | Index of every page produced by one dream cycle. Auto-written deterministically by the orchestrator. |
148	
149	**Iron Law for synthesize output:**
150	1. Quote the user verbatim. Do not paraphrase memorable phrasings.
151	2. Cross-reference compulsively: every new page MUST link to existing brain content.
152	3. Slug discipline: lowercase alphanumeric and hyphens only, slash-separated. NO underscores, NO file extensions.
153	4. Edited transcripts produce NEW slugs (content-hash suffix changes) — never silently overwrite a prior reflection.
154	
155	## Takes attribution (v0.32+)
156	
157	When writing a `<!--- gbrain:takes:begin -->` fence, the **holder** column says
158	WHO BELIEVES the claim, not who it's ABOUT. Cross-modal eval over 100K
159	production takes scored attribution at 6.5/10 — holder/subject confusion was
160	the #1 error. These six rules are the contract. Long form with worked
161	examples lives in `docs/takes-vs-facts.md`.
162	
163	1. **Holder ≠ subject.** The test: did this person SAY or CLEARLY IMPLY this?
164	   - YES → `holder = people/<slug>`
165	   - NO, it's your analysis OF them → `holder = brain`
166	   - Example: "Garry has a hero/rescuer pattern" → `holder=brain` (analysis ABOUT Garry, not stated BY Garry)
167	2. **Atomic claims.** Split compound rows into separate rows. One claim per row.
168	3. **Amplification ≠ endorsement.** A retweet-only signal caps at `weight 0.55`.
169	   The user shared something; they didn't necessarily endorse every clause.
170	4. **Self-reported ≠ verified.** "Saif reports 7 figures" → `holder=people/saif`,
171	   `weight=0.75`, NOT `holder=world/1.0`. Self-report is a strong individual
172	   signal, not consensus fact.
173	5. **No false precision.** Use 0.05 increments only (`0.35`, `0.55`, `0.75`).
174	   `0.74` and `0.82` imply calibration accuracy that doesn't exist. The engine
175	   layer rounds on insert — match the grid in your fence and avoid the warning.
176	6. **"So what" test.** Skip metadata-style trivia (Twitter handles, follower
177	   counts, obvious bio fields). A take has to be load-bearing for some future
178	   query.
179	
180	**Holder format (enforced as a parser warning in v0.32, error in v0.33+):**
181	- `world` (consensus fact, no individual claimant)
182	- `brain` (AI-inferred, holder genuinely ambiguous)
183	- `people/<slug>` (individual's stated belief)
184	- `companies/<slug>` (institutional fact, no individual claimant)
185	
186	Slugs use the standard grammar (`[a-z0-9._-]+`). `Garry`, `people/Garry-Tan`,
187	and `world/garry-tan` all fail validation.
188	
189	**Founder-describing-own-company rule.** When a founder describes their own
190	company, the holder is the FOUNDER, not the company. "We can hit $10M ARR"
191	said by Bo Lu → `holder=people/bo-lu`, NOT `holder=companies/clipboard-health`.
192	Companies don't speak; their employees do.

# RESOLVER — Master Routing Rules

**Read this file before creating or moving ANY page.** It is the single
authority for *where* knowledge lands. `schema.md` governs *how* a page is
shaped. Every piece of knowledge resolves to exactly one canonical file.

## Decision Order

1. Is it **sensitive** (assessment, performance review, personal feedback,
   compensation)? → `sensitive/` and STOP. See §Sensitive.
2. Is it a **person**? → `people/first-last.md`.
3. Is it a **company / employer / vendor / interview target / consulting
   client**? → `companies/<slug>.md`.
4. Is it a **meeting / transcript / session note**? → `meetings/` (synthesized)
   or `sources/` (raw). See §Meetings.
5. Is it a **project** (active work, deliverables, owner, dates)? →
   `projects/<scope>/<slug>.md`.
6. Is it a **concept** (reusable framework, mental model, study material,
   instructional)? → `concepts/<slug>.md`.
7. Is it an **idea** (productive/generative output, proposals, writing)? →
   `ideas/<slug>.md`.
8. Is it **career/org structure** (ladders, principles, STAR stories)? →
   `organization/<slug>.md`.
9. Is it a **dated work log**? → `journal/YYYY/...`.
10. Is it **vault-tooling / operational documentation** (GBrain/Hermes config,
    scripts, automation procedures — not career/org content)? → `ops/`;
    dated operational logs specifically → `ops/logs/`.
11. Is it a **personal reflective essay** (point-in-time, non-cumulative
    processing — self-knowledge, emotional processing, pattern recognition)?
    → `reflections/<slug>.md`.
12. Is it a **cross-session theme/pattern** (recurring signal detected across
    ≥3 reflections)? → `patterns/<slug>.md`.
13. Otherwise → `archive/` (historical) or `inbox/` (unresolved — flag it).

## Concept vs. Project (the hard call)

- **Concept** = *instructional / reusable / timeless*. Teaches a method, holds
  a framework, transferable across contexts. No owner, no due date.
  *e.g. "Data strategy framework", "Training a multimodal LLM" (pedagogical).*
- **Project** = *productive / time-bound / owned*. Has a goal, stakeholders,
  status, dated execution log. Specific to one effort.
  *e.g. "AI Planning roadmap", "Atlas dashboard", "train the building-code model".*

When a source file mixes both, **`split`** it: thesis → `concepts/`, execution
log → `projects/`.

## Linking

When establishing links among files, **DO NOT USE relative links** — always reference
an absolute path from the root of the vault.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# KB pre-commit hook — guards brain entity pages against destructive overwrites.
#
# Brain pages are a cumulative ledger: Compiled Truth is re-synthesized, but
# Timeline entries and YAML frontmatter must never be silently dropped. This
# catches the "Scorealytics Regression" class of bug — a full-file rewrite that
# regenerates a page from only the newest source and nukes prior content.
# See .hermes/skills/conventions/quality.md → "Page-Update Discipline".
#
# Override when a large deletion is INTENTIONAL (prune / archive / merge / split):
#   ALLOW_ENTITY_SHRINK=1 git commit ...

set -u

GUARDED_RE='^(companies|concepts|journal|media|meetings|people|projects)/.*\.md$'
SHRINK_PCT=60     # flag if new body <= 60% of old (i.e. >40% of lines lost)
MIN_OLD_LINES=20  # ignore small files where a big % swing is normal
flagged=0

# Count YAML frontmatter keys between the first two '---' fences.
yaml_keys() {
  awk 'NR==1 && $0=="---"{inside=1; next}
       inside && $0=="---"{exit}
       inside && /^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+:/{c++}
       END{print c+0}'
}
line_count() { wc -l | tr -d ' '; }

while IFS="$(printf '\t')" read -r status path _rest; do

Use whenever new facts about an already-noted person, company, project, or topic need to land on its existing page.
