---
title: Add relationship/graph-traversal queries (backfills ADR 0006 too)
status: proposal
audience: wakil coding agent
---

# Add relationship/graph-traversal queries to `wakil query`

## Problem

Two related gaps surfaced while building a kb-side skill (`wakil-query`)
that shells out to `wakil search`/`wakil query`:

1. **ADR 0006's backlinks were never actually wired up.** ADR 0006 ("Backlinks
   as a Live Query Over a Widened Relationship Table") designed
   `Relationship.subject_note_id`/`object_note_id` for exactly this, and the
   schema/migration exist. But grepping the real application code
   (`src/wakil/app/*.py`) turns up exactly one place a `Relationship` row is
   ever constructed — `ingest_service.py`'s `apply_enrichment`, and it's
   `subject_memory_id`/`object_memory_id` only. The note-note columns are
   exercised solely by `tests/unit/test_migrations.py::test_note_to_note_relationship_roundtrip`,
   a hand-constructed unit test. **In the real, current system, no backlink
   is ever automatic — for wakil-authored content or hand-edited content.**
   Every downstream doc/skill that assumed otherwise (this kb's `CLAUDE.md`,
   `wakil-query`, `enrich`, `quickcapture-ingest`) has been corrected to say
   so plainly (2026-07-23) pending this work.
2. **No relationship/graph-traversal at all.** Even once backlinks are real,
   they'd only be generic "these two notes are linked" edges. There's no way
   to ask a typed, structural question — "who works at Acme?", "who has
   Alice met (via meetings)?" — the way the retired gbrain system's
   `graph-query --type works_at --direction in` could.

## Two build in one pass, deliberately

Phase 1 below is not new scope creep bolted onto a graph-traversal feature —
it's finishing what ADR 0006 already decided and never landed. Phase 2 is
the actual new capability. Doing both together is smaller than it looks,
since Phase 2's traversal only becomes meaningful once Phase 1 populates
real edges.

## Design decision: wikilink extraction belongs in *indexing*, not enrichment

The obvious first instinct is to populate `Relationship` rows during
`wakil enrich`'s own entity-resolution step, alongside the existing
`subject_memory_id`/`object_memory_id` writes. **Don't** — that would only
ever cover content that went through `wakil ingest`/`enrich`, permanently
reproducing the exact "hand-edits don't get backlinks" gap this kb's
`CLAUDE.md` currently documents as an accepted limitation. It doesn't have
to be permanent.

Instead: extend `index_notes()` (`src/wakil/app/workspace_service.py`) — the
same deterministic, no-model-call pass that already syncs the `Note` table
with what's on disk on every `wakil index`/`wakil init` — to also parse each
note body for `[[wikilink]]` targets and upsert generic `Relationship` rows
for them. Consequences of this choice:

- **Every indexed note gets link extraction, hand-edited or wakil-authored,
  old or new**, the next time anyone runs `wakil index`. No separate
  backfill command needed for the existing 2,700+ note corpus — a plain
  reindex covers it.
- The predicate at index time must be something derivable **without a model
  call**, since indexing is cheap and runs constantly — a single generic
  predicate (`mentions`, matching the existing free-string convention on
  `Relationship.predicate`) is all indexing can respformsonsibly claim. This
  is enough to make backlinks (ADR 0006's original goal) actually real.
- Typed, semantic predicates (`works_at`, `founded`, `advises`, `attended`)
  are a **separate, optional** enhancement — Phase 2 below — layered on top
  once generic edges exist, not a blocker for shipping Phase 1.

### Phase 1 — generic Note↔Note edges at index time

1. In `index_notes()`, after upserting/updating a `Note` row, parse its
   current body for `[[path]]` / `[[path|display]]` wikilinks (reuse the
   existing wikilink-form logic already in `ingest_service.py` —
   `_reconcile_note_links`'s neighborhood already parses this shape for
   note-conformance corrections; don't re-derive the regex).
2. Resolve each wikilink target to an existing `Note` row by path (both
   `[[people/x]]` and `[[sources/y.md]]` forms appear for real in this kb,
   per `ingest_service.py`'s own comment — resolve both). A target that
   doesn't resolve to a real note is not an error here — dead-link
   detection is `maintain`'s job, not indexing's; skip silently.
3. Upsert a `Relationship(subject_note_id=<this note>, predicate="mentions",
   object_note_id=<target note>, workspace_id=...)` row — idempotent (dedupe
   on subject/predicate/object so re-indexing an unchanged note is a no-op,
   matching `index_notes()`'s existing unchanged/updated/added counting).
4. On re-index, if a note's wikilinks changed (some removed), remove the
   `Relationship` rows for targets no longer mentioned — mirrors
   `index_notes()`'s existing prune semantics for removed notes.
5. No migration needed — the columns already exist (migration `0002`).

### Phase 2 — typed entity relationships + query surface

1. Extend `wakil enrich`'s entity-resolution output (optionally, only when
   it already resolves two entities together in the same source) with a
   proposed relationship type from a small, free-string-not-fixed-enum
   vocabulary (matching the existing `CandidateRelationshipModel.predicate`
   convention of a described-not-enforced set: `works_at | founded | advises
   | attended | invested_in | mentions`). This reuses an existing model call
   (no new LLM cost) and only covers content going through `wakil enrich` —
   fine, since Phase 1's generic `mentions` edges already give full-corpus
   coverage as a fallback.
2. Add a query surface — a new `wakil relationships <note-path>` command
   (or a `--related`/`--graph` mode on `wakil query`, naming TBD): given a
   note, list linked notes filtered by `--predicate <type>` and
   `--direction in|out|both`, with `--depth N` for multi-hop traversal via a
   SQLite `WITH RECURSIVE` CTE over `Relationship` scoped to note ids — no
   new graph library or database, matching the project's existing bias
   (`CLAUDE.md`: "avoid premature graph databases") since this reuses the
   table ADR 0006 already widened rather than introducing new
   infrastructure.
3. `wakil-query` (the kb-side skill) gets updated once this ships to
   document the new command and retire its current "real gap" disclaimer.

## Open questions

- **Predicate vocabulary**: free string (matches `CandidateRelationshipModel`'s
  existing convention, simplest) vs. a small fixed set enforced at the
  schema layer (more consistent, more upfront work; `Relationship.predicate`
  today is `String(50)`, unconstrained either way). Lean free string,
  consistent with how `memory_type`/`stance` were handled (ADR 0013/0014) —
  don't add enforcement until it's shown to be needed.
- **Depth bound for traversal**: cap the recursive CTE at a fixed max depth
  (e.g. 5, matching gbrain's old default) to avoid runaway queries on a
  densely-linked kb — needs picking, not derived from anything in wakil today.
- **Should Phase 2's typed-relationship extraction be its own model call**
  (more accurate, an added cost) **or folded into existing entity-resolution
  output** (free, but entity-resolution's current job is narrowly "does this
  refer to an existing page," not "what's the relationship type" — scope
  creep on that skill's stated boundary, see `entity-resolution/SKILL.md`).
  Lean toward folding in only if it doesn't blur that skill's contract;
  otherwise a dedicated pass, deferred until Phase 1 alone is shown
  insufficient — mirrors the phase-1-before-phase-2 discipline ADR 0013/0014
  already used for the memory-register work.
- **Command name/shape** for the query surface — `wakil relationships`,
  or a mode on `wakil query` — no strong opinion yet, pick whichever reads
  better once Phase 1 exists to test it against real data.

## Acceptance criteria (Phase 1 only — Phase 2 is a separate follow-up)

- [ ] `index_notes()` extracts `[[wikilinks]]` into generic `mentions`
      `Relationship` rows, idempotently, on every `wakil index`/`init`.
- [ ] Re-indexing an unchanged note doesn't duplicate or churn rows.
- [ ] Removing a wikilink from a note removes the corresponding row on
      next reindex.
- [ ] Both `[[people/x]]` and `[[sources/y.md]]` wikilink forms resolve.
- [ ] A wikilink to a nonexistent note is skipped, not an error.
- [ ] Tests cover: fresh index populates edges; unchanged reindex is a
      no-op; removed link prunes its row; both wikilink forms resolve;
      a dead-link target is skipped cleanly.
- [ ] This kb's `CLAUDE.md`/`wakil-query`/`enrich`/`quickcapture-ingest`
      corrections (2026-07-23, "not wired up yet") get a follow-up update
      once Phase 1 ships, since the gap they document will be closed.

---
name: maintain
description: "First-pass kb health check: orphan pages, dead links (wikilink + markdown forms), tag consistency, stale-content detection (wakil-DB-backed where possible), citation spot-check, index drift. File-grep plus targeted read-only wakil DB queries, no gbrain. Use for 'brain health', 'check backlinks', 'orphan pages', 'stale pages', 'kb maintenance'. A genuinely new, first-pass tool, not a full reconciliation of the old gbrain-based maintain skill — several of its dimensions (embedding freshness, RLS, dream-cycle, file-storage routing) don't apply to wakil's architecture at all and are intentionally dropped, not silently ported."
skill_api: 1
---

# maintain

A first-pass health check for the kb: mostly grep/file-based, with a few
targeted **read-only** queries against wakil's own SQLite store
(`.wakil/wakil.db`) where that's genuinely more reliable than grepping —
never a write, only ever via `wakil` CLI commands where one exists. This is
new tooling, not a port of the old gbrain-based `maintain` skill — that
skill's embedding-freshness, RLS, dream-cycle, and file-storage-redirect
checks don't apply to wakil's architecture at all and are dropped, not
silently carried forward.

## Where the wakil DB actually helps (and where it doesn't)

**Doesn't help — orphan/backlink detection.** wakil's `Relationship` table
has `subject_note_id`/`object_note_id` columns designed for exactly this
(ADR 0006), but as of 2026-07-23 **nothing populates them** — verified
against `src/wakil/app/ingest_service.py`, the only real `Relationship`
writes are memory↔memory, never note↔note (see
`docs/relationship-graph-traversal-proposal.md` in `~/Projects/wakil` for
the fix). Querying the DB for orphans/backlinks today would report
*everything* as orphaned — worse than useless. Grep across the actual
Markdown is the only source of truth for links until that ships.

**Does help — dead-link resolution.** wakil's `Note` table is the
authoritative, already-indexed list of every real note path (populated by
`wakil index`/`init`). Resolving a wikilink target against it is more
reliable than guessing a filesystem path yourself (handles date-prefixed
slugs, directory conventions, etc. the way wakil's own indexer already
worked out). Read-only:
```bash
sqlite3 .wakil/wakil.db "SELECT path FROM notes WHERE workspace_id = <id>;"
```
Compare each wikilink target against this list rather than `test -f`-ing a
guessed path.

**Does help — stale-content detection, and better than a heuristic.** A
note with `Memory` rows linked to it (`note_id`) in `state='candidate'`
(i.e. proposed by `wakil enrich` but never promoted) that are newer than
the note's own last edit is a **precise** signal that new information
exists and hasn't been fully synthesized in — much better than parsing
Timeline dates out of prose. Read-only:
```bash
sqlite3 .wakil/wakil.db \
  "SELECT note_id, COUNT(*) FROM memories
   WHERE workspace_id = <id> AND state = 'candidate' AND note_id IS NOT NULL
   GROUP BY note_id;"
```
Use the prose-Timeline-vs-frontmatter heuristic (below) only as a fallback
for notes with no linked memories at all (e.g. entirely hand-authored).

**Does help — index drift, a bonus check the old skill didn't have.**
`wakil status`'s reported `Notes indexed` count comes from the `Note` table,
not a live filesystem scan — if someone hand-edited files without running
`wakil index` afterward, the DB can drift from disk. Compare:
```bash
wakil -w kb status   # note_count from the DB
find . -name '*.md' | wc -l   # actual files (adjust for excluded paths)
```
A mismatch means run `wakil -w kb index` before trusting anything else in
this report.

## What this checks (mechanical, reliable)

### Orphan pages

A page under a guarded entity directory (`people/`, `companies/`,
`concepts/`, `projects/`) with zero inbound references anywhere in the
vault. **Check both link forms `RESOLVER.md` permits** — this kb uses
wikilinks *and* absolute markdown-path links (`[text](companies/regtime.md)`),
not just `[[wikilinks]]`; a check for only one form produces false-positive
orphans.

```bash
# Wikilink form: [[slug]] or [[slug|Display]]
grep -rl "\[\[.*<slug>" --include="*.md" .
# Markdown form: [text](path/to/slug.md)
grep -rl "](.*<slug>\.md)" --include="*.md" .
```

Combine both result sets (excluding the page's own file) — empty combined
result = orphan. Report it; don't delete or auto-link — ask whether it's
genuinely isolated (fine, e.g. a fresh stub) or should be linked from
somewhere.

### Dead links

A link (either form above) pointing at a path with no corresponding file.
Resolve against the `Note` table (see above) rather than guessing a
filesystem path. Report dead links; don't remove them without checking
whether the target was renamed/moved (fix the link) vs. genuinely never
existed (remove or flag for the user).

### Tag consistency

Collect every `tags:` frontmatter value across the vault; look for
near-duplicate variants (case differences, singular/plural, hyphen vs.
no-hyphen — e.g. `vc` vs `venture-capital`, `ai` vs `artificial-intelligence`).
Report clusters of likely-duplicate tags; standardizing is a judgment call
for the user, not something to auto-fix.

### Stale content

Prefer the DB-backed candidate-memory check above. Fall back to the
heuristic only when a page has no linked memories: compare the newest
dated Timeline entry against the file's frontmatter `updated:` field — if
the Timeline has moved meaningfully past `updated:`, flag it as "worth a
look," not a confirmed defect. A human still decides whether re-synthesis
(via `note-revision`) is warranted.

### Index drift

See above — `wakil status`'s note count vs. an actual file count.

## What this checks (judgment-call, not mechanical)

### Citation spot-check

Read a sample of recently-modified pages (`git log --since=<N days> --name-only -- 'people/*.md' 'companies/*.md'`,
or similar) and check that substantive claims in Compiled Truth carry a
`(reported: X)` / `(self-reported)` tag (wakil's convention, not the legacy

Nothing is automatic today (see above) — for any recent edit, hand-edited
or `wakil`-authored, check whether an entity it mentions should have a
back-link line pointing to it, and whether that line exists. This requires
reading both pages, not a grep pattern; revisit once
`docs/relationship-graph-traversal-proposal.md` ships.

## A note on the entity-shrink git hook

`.githooks/pre-commit` blocks a commit that shrinks a guarded entity page
by >40% or drops a YAML key — this will fire during legitimate
prune/archive/merge/split operations, not just accidental clobbering. If
`maintain` (or anything else) proposes an intentional large deletion,
the override is `ALLOW_ENTITY_SHRINK=1 git commit ...` — don't treat a hook
rejection as unconditionally wrong, but don't reach for the override
without confirming the shrink really is intentional first.

Filing-rule violations (content in `sources/` that has a clear primary
subject and should be filed elsewhere) requires reading the content and
applying `RESOLVER.md`'s primary-subject judgment — there's no reliable
keyword heuristic for this. Sample a few `sources/` files and apply the
judgment by hand if asked; don't script a fake check.

Embedding freshness, RLS/security status, schema migration health,
dream-cycle diagnostics, file-storage redirect integrity, search-quality
benchmarks (Tier 1–4 query batteries) — all gbrain-specific, not
applicable to wakil. If asked for one of these, say plainly that wakil
doesn't have an equivalent rather than faking a result.

| Dimension | Checked | Issues found |

| Dead links | Y | N |

| Citation spot-check (sample of M pages) | Y | N gaps |
| Backlinks (manual check) | Y (if any edits since last run) | N missing |
| Index drift | Y | note_count vs. file count |

### Details
[Per-dimension: specific pages/links/tags found, with paths]

### Explicitly not checked (out of scope for wakil)
Embedding freshness, RLS, schema migration health, dream-cycle, file
storage integrity, search benchmarks.

### Outstanding issues for you to decide
[Anything needing a judgment call — don't auto-fix these]

- Auto-fixing anything (deleting orphans, removing dead links, merging

- Presenting a heuristic (stale content fallback) or a sample (citation
  spot-check) as if it were an exhaustive, certain result.
- Inventing a mechanical check for a dimension that genuinely needs human

15

# Build prompt: docs/relationship-graph-traversal-proposal.md

You are implementing `docs/relationship-graph-traversal-proposal.md` in the
`wakil` repo. **Before writing any code**, read, in full:

1. `docs/relationship-graph-traversal-proposal.md` — the spec for this work.
2. `docs/DEVELOPMENT.md` — recurring dev patterns this repo has already
   learned the hard way. Every pattern in it applies to this work if it's
   touched by what you're doing; the most directly relevant ones are called
   out per-workstream below, but read the whole file, not just those.
3. These ADRs, in this order of relevance:
   - `docs/adr/0006-backlinks-as-live-query-over-widened-relationship-table.md` —
     the decision this proposal finishes implementing.
   - `docs/adr/0008-ingestion-decomposition-reject-multi-agent-mechanism.md` —
     **read this one carefully; see the note below before assuming anything
     about "concurrent agents."**
   - `docs/adr/0005-timeline-entries-as-memory-rows.md` and
     `docs/adr/0007-markdown-source-of-truth-sqlite-operational-store.md` —
     establish the "reuse existing tables, Markdown is truth, SQLite is
     operational cache" precedent this proposal follows (no new tables, no
     new graph database/library).
   - `docs/adr/0013-opinion-memory-type-and-confidence-ranking.md` and
     `docs/adr/0014-memory-register-field-and-query-exclusion.md` — the most
     recent example of this repo's own phased-feature-plus-ADR discipline
     (phase 1 before phase 2, an ADR written at the end citing real
     file:line evidence, acceptance criteria checked off, not asserted).
     Match this rigor, including writing the final ADR (`0015-...md` — check
     `docs/adr/` for the actual next-free number before you file it in case
     something else has landed first) once implementation is done and
     verified, not before.
4. `CLAUDE.md`'s "Design Biases" section (`Avoid`: large agent frameworks,
   multi-agent orchestration, hidden background behavior, premature graph
   databases). This proposal's Phase 2 query surface is a SQL `WITH
   RECURSIVE` CTE over the existing `Relationship` table — if you find
   yourself reaching for a graph library, a new database, or an
   agent-decided traversal strategy, stop; that violates this repo's stated
   design bias and this proposal's own reasoning for why it isn't scope
   creep.

## Critical: "many concurrent agents" means dev-process parallelism, not runtime architecture

ADR 0008 rejected a multi-agent *mechanism* for how `wakil`'s ingestion
pipeline makes decisions at use-time — classification, extraction, entity
resolution, and enforcement are a **fixed, code-sequenced DAG**, never
agent-decided control flow. Nothing in this build should introduce
agent-decided runtime behavior into that pipeline or into the new graph
feature. The "many agents concurrently" instruction is about **how this
implementation work gets divided across multiple simultaneous Claude Code
sessions** (parallelizing the build), not about making the shipped feature
itself multi-agent. If anything in your plan would make `wakil`'s own
runtime behavior agent-decided rather than code-sequenced, stop and ask
before implementing it — that's exactly the mechanism ADR 0008 rejected.

## Workstreams (claim one, work on its own branch, open its own PR)

Each workstream owns a distinct set of files. Before starting, check open
branches/PRs for `feat/graph-*` naming to see what's already claimed or
in progress — don't duplicate another agent's work. Workstreams B and C can
run in parallel with A once A's Relationship-table shape is confirmed
unchanged (it isn't changing — no migration needed, per the proposal). D is
strictly last; it depends on A, B, and C all being merged.

### Workstream A — Phase 1: index-time wikilink extraction (foundational)

**Owns:** `src/wakil/app/workspace_service.py` (`index_notes()`), a new
small pure-function module for wikilink parsing/resolution (your choice of
name/location, but keep it dependency-free and independently testable —
don't fold parsing logic directly into `index_notes()`'s body), and its own
tests (`tests/unit/test_migrations.py` already has the closest existing
pattern — `test_note_to_note_relationship_roundtrip` — extend that file or
add a sibling one, your call).

Implements the proposal's Phase 1 exactly as specified: parse `[[wikilink]]`
targets (both `[[path]]` and `[[path|display]]`, both `[[people/x]]` and
`[[sources/y.md]]` forms — reuse the existing wikilink-form logic already in
`ingest_service.py` near `_reconcile_note_links` rather than re-deriving the
regex), resolve against the `Note` table, upsert idempotent `mentions`
`Relationship` rows, prune rows for links removed on re-index. Meet every
acceptance-criteria checkbox in the proposal's Phase 1 section — they're
specific and testable, don't skip any.

**DEVELOPMENT.md patterns that apply here:** none of the existing entries
are a close match to this specific change, but if you find yourself writing
a longer-running backfill/reindex path with real cost or failure risk,
apply the "print diagnostic detail as it happens" pattern anyway — an
interrupted reindex on a large vault should still leave a legible partial
result, not silence until a final summary.

### Workstream B — Phase 2a: typed relationship extraction during enrich

**Owns:** `src/wakil/skills/entity-resolution/SKILL.md`,
`src/wakil/skills/entity-resolution/eval.json`, whatever schema addition in
`src/wakil/llm/schemas.py` is needed to carry a proposed relationship type
alongside an existing entity resolution, and the corresponding wiring in
`src/wakil/app/ingest_service.py`'s entity-resolution DAG step.

**This workstream has real open questions the proposal explicitly flags as
unresolved — do not silently pick an answer:**
- Free-string predicate vocabulary (matching `CandidateRelationshipModel`'s
  existing convention) vs. a fixed enum. The proposal leans free-string;
  confirm before building the other way.
- Whether typed-relationship extraction folds into `entity-resolution`'s
  existing model call (free, but risks blurring that skill's stated
  contract — read `entity-resolution/SKILL.md`'s own "keep the two separate"
  framing before deciding) or is a dedicated pass. The proposal leans
  "fold in only if it doesn't blur the contract, otherwise defer" — this is
  a judgment call on actual `SKILL.md` prose, not a default to assume.

If you can pause and ask the user, do so before committing to either
answer. If running unattended, take the proposal's stated lean, but put an
unmissable "ASSUMPTION MADE — NEEDS REVIEW" section at the top of your PR
description naming exactly what you decided and why, so a human catches it
before merge rather than after.

**DEVELOPMENT.md patterns that apply here — all of them, directly:**
- "Run the live eval before treating new SKILL.md guidance as done" — you
  are editing `entity-resolution/SKILL.md` and its `eval.json`. Writing the
  scenario is not the finish line; `uv run pytest -m eval -k <scenario id>`
  actually passing against a real model call is.
- "A skill's `references/*.md` files are never loaded into the model's

  precedes what it's meant to gate.
- "A full live-model eval-suite run has a high baseline failure rate" — if

  compare against a same-day `main` baseline rather than reading the raw
  failure count; a single targeted scenario re-run is a more reliable

### Workstream C — Phase 2b: query surface (traversal command)

**Owns:** a new CLI command in `src/wakil/cli/main.py` (name/shape is an
open question below), a new service module for the traversal query (SQLite
`WITH RECURSIVE` CTE over `Relationship`, scoped by note id, `--predicate`,
`--direction in|out|both`, `--depth N`), display wiring in
`src/wakil/ui/console.py`, and its own tests. Can be built and unit-tested
against directly-seeded `Relationship` rows (the schema already exists,

**Open question, don't guess silently:** command name/shape — a new

on the existing `wakil query`. Ask the user if you can; if unattended, pick
whichever reads more naturally given how `wakil query`/`wakil search` are
already structured, and flag the choice prominently in your PR description.

**Also open:** the recursive traversal's max-depth cap (the proposal
suggests 5 as a starting point, matching the retired gbrain system's old
default, but states this isn't derived from anything in `wakil` itself —
confirm rather than assume it's the right number for this workload).

### Workstream D — Integration, docs, and the ADR (sequential, last)

**Depends on A, B, and C all being merged.** Owns: end-to-end tests
exercising the full flow (index → extract → traverse), `README.md` updates,
and the final `docs/adr/00NN-*.md` (check the actual next-free number in
`docs/adr/` at the time you write it) — written the way `0013`/`0014` were:
cite real file:line evidence for what actually shipped, not what was
planned, and don't claim something works until you've verified it against

Also: once Phase 1 is merged and working, go update
`~/Projects/kb/CLAUDE.md`, `~/Projects/kb/skills/wakil-query/SKILL.md`,
`~/Projects/kb/skills/enrich/SKILL.md`, and
`~/Projects/kb/skills/quickcapture-ingest/SKILL.md` — all four currently

   touched by what you're doing; the most directly relevant ones are called
   out per-workstream below, but read the whole file, not just those.
3. These ADRs, in this order of relevance:
   - `docs/adr/0006-backlinks-as-live-query-over-widened-relationship-table.md` —
     the decision this proposal finishes implementing.
   - `docs/adr/0008-ingestion-decomposition-reject-multi-agent-mechanism.md` —
     **read this one carefully; see the note below before assuming anything
     about "concurrent agents."**
   - `docs/adr/0005-timeline-entries-as-memory-rows.md` and
     `docs/adr/0007-markdown-source-of-truth-sqlite-operational-store.md` —
     establish the "reuse existing tables, Markdown is truth, SQLite is

     new graph database/library).
   - `docs/adr/0013-opinion-memory-type-and-confidence-ranking.md` and
     `docs/adr/0014-memory-register-field-and-query-exclusion.md` — the most
     recent example of this repo's own phased-feature-plus-ADR discipline
     (phase 1 before phase 2, an ADR written at the end citing real

4. `CLAUDE.md`'s "Design Biases" section (`Avoid`: large agent frameworks,

   agent-decided traversal strategy, stop; that violates this repo's stated
   design bias and this proposal's own reasoning for why it isn't scope
   creep.

## Critical: "many concurrent agents" means dev-process parallelism, not runtime architecture

ADR 0008 rejected a multi-agent *mechanism* for how `wakil`'s ingestion
pipeline makes decisions at use-time — classification, extraction, entity
resolution, and enforcement are a **fixed, code-sequenced DAG**, never
agent-decided control flow. Nothing in this build should introduce
agent-decided runtime behavior into that pipeline or into the new graph
feature. The "many agents concurrently" instruction is about **how this
implementation work gets divided across multiple simultaneous Claude Code
sessions** (parallelizing the build), not about making the shipped feature
itself multi-agent. If anything in your plan would make `wakil`'s own
runtime behavior agent-decided rather than code-sequenced, stop and ask
before implementing it — that's exactly the mechanism ADR 0008 rejected.

## Workstreams (claim one, work on its own branch, open its own PR)

Each workstream owns a distinct set of files. Before starting, check open
branches/PRs for `feat/graph-*` naming to see what's already claimed or
in progress — don't duplicate another agent's work. Workstreams B and C can
run in parallel with A once A's Relationship-table shape is confirmed
unchanged (it isn't changing — no migration needed, per the proposal). D is
strictly last; it depends on A, B, and C all being merged.

### Workstream A — Phase 1: index-time wikilink extraction (foundational)

**Owns:** `src/wakil/app/workspace_service.py` (`index_notes()`), a new
small pure-function module for wikilink parsing/resolution (your choice of
name/location, but keep it dependency-free and independently testable —
don't fold parsing logic directly into `index_notes()`'s body), and its own
tests (`tests/unit/test_migrations.py` already has the closest existing
pattern — `test_note_to_note_relationship_roundtrip` — extend that file or
add a sibling one, your call).

Implements the proposal's Phase 1 exactly as specified: parse `[[wikilink]]`
targets (both `[[path]]` and `[[path|display]]`, both `[[people/x]]` and
`[[sources/y.md]]` forms — reuse the existing wikilink-form logic already in
`ingest_service.py` near `_reconcile_note_links` rather than re-deriving the
regex), resolve against the `Note` table, upsert idempotent `mentions`
`Relationship` rows, prune rows for links removed on re-index. Meet every
acceptance-criteria checkbox in the proposal's Phase 1 section — they're
specific and testable, don't skip any.

**DEVELOPMENT.md patterns that apply here:** none of the existing entries
are a close match to this specific change, but if you find yourself writing
a longer-running backfill/reindex path with real cost or failure risk,
apply the "print diagnostic detail as it happens" pattern anyway — an
interrupted reindex on a large vault should still leave a legible partial
result, not silence until a final summary.

### Workstream B — Phase 2a: typed relationship extraction during enrich

**Owns:** `src/wakil/skills/entity-resolution/SKILL.md`,
`src/wakil/skills/entity-resolution/eval.json`, whatever schema addition in
`src/wakil/llm/schemas.py` is needed to carry a proposed relationship type
alongside an existing entity resolution, and the corresponding wiring in
`src/wakil/app/ingest_service.py`'s entity-resolution DAG step.

**This workstream has real open questions the proposal explicitly flags as
unresolved — do not silently pick an answer:**
- Free-string predicate vocabulary (matching `CandidateRelationshipModel`'s
  existing convention) vs. a fixed enum. The proposal leans free-string;
  confirm before building the other way.
- Whether typed-relationship extraction folds into `entity-resolution`'s
  existing model call (free, but risks blurring that skill's stated
  contract — read `entity-resolution/SKILL.md`'s own "keep the two separate"
  framing before deciding) or is a dedicated pass. The proposal leans
  "fold in only if it doesn't blur the contract, otherwise defer" — this is
  a judgment call on actual `SKILL.md` prose, not a default to assume.

If you can pause and ask the user, do so before committing to either
answer. If running unattended, take the proposal's stated lean, but put an
unmissable "ASSUMPTION MADE — NEEDS REVIEW" section at the top of your PR
description naming exactly what you decided and why, so a human catches it
before merge rather than after.

**DEVELOPMENT.md patterns that apply here — all of them, directly:**
- "Run the live eval before treating new SKILL.md guidance as done" — you
  are editing `entity-resolution/SKILL.md` and its `eval.json`. Writing the
  scenario is not the finish line; `uv run pytest -m eval -k <scenario id>`
  actually passing against a real model call is.
- "A skill's `references/*.md` files are never loaded into the model's
  context" — if the new relationship-type guidance needs to actually affect
  model behavior, it must live in `SKILL.md`'s own body, not a `references/`
  file, no matter how clearly `SKILL.md` points at one.
- "Check whether a skill's own procedure step order can produce the bug
  it's trying to prevent" — if you add a step to `entity-resolution`'s
  decision procedure, check it's ordered so any gate/check step actually
  precedes what it's meant to gate.
- "A full live-model eval-suite run has a high baseline failure rate" — if
  you run the complete `-m eval` suite to sanity-check nothing regressed,
  compare against a same-day `main` baseline rather than reading the raw
  failure count; a single targeted scenario re-run is a more reliable
  signal than the full sweep.

### Workstream C — Phase 2b: query surface (traversal command)

**Owns:** a new CLI command in `src/wakil/cli/main.py` (name/shape is an
open question below), a new service module for the traversal query (SQLite
`WITH RECURSIVE` CTE over `Relationship`, scoped by note id, `--predicate`,
`--direction in|out|both`, `--depth N`), display wiring in
`src/wakil/ui/console.py`, and its own tests. Can be built and unit-tested
against directly-seeded `Relationship` rows (the schema already exists,
unchanged) without waiting on Workstream A's real extraction code —
integration testing against real extracted edges happens in Workstream D.

**Open question, don't guess silently:** command name/shape — a new
`wakil relationships <note-path>` command, or a `--related`/`--graph` mode
on the existing `wakil query`. Ask the user if you can; if unattended, pick
whichever reads more naturally given how `wakil query`/`wakil search` are
already structured, and flag the choice prominently in your PR description.

**Also open:** the recursive traversal's max-depth cap (the proposal
suggests 5 as a starting point, matching the retired gbrain system's old
default, but states this isn't derived from anything in `wakil` itself —
confirm rather than assume it's the right number for this workload).

### Workstream D — Integration, docs, and the ADR (sequential, last)

**Depends on A, B, and C all being merged.** Owns: end-to-end tests
exercising the full flow (index → extract → traverse), `README.md` updates,
and the final `docs/adr/00NN-*.md` (check the actual next-free number in
`docs/adr/` at the time you write it) — written the way `0013`/`0014` were:
cite real file:line evidence for what actually shipped, not what was
planned, and don't claim something works until you've verified it against
the real code and a real test run, the same discipline this repo's own
session history (see `docs/DEVELOPMENT.md`) had to learn by getting burned
by the opposite.

Also: once Phase 1 is merged and working, go update
`~/Projects/kb/CLAUDE.md`, `~/Projects/kb/skills/wakil-query/SKILL.md`,
`~/Projects/kb/skills/enrich/SKILL.md`, and
`~/Projects/kb/skills/quickcapture-ingest/SKILL.md` — all four currently
carry an explicit "corrected 2026-07-23: not wired up yet" note about
backlinks not being automatic, written in anticipation of this exact work
landing. That correction needs a follow-up correction once it's no longer
true. Don't skip this step — it's a real, separate repo (a personal
knowledge-base vault, not `wakil` itself), and it's the actual reason this
feature was scoped in the first place.

## General rules for every workstream

- Ask when genuinely ambiguous — this document calls out the known open
  questions above, but if you hit another one (an untested assumption about
  existing code, a design choice the proposal doesn't resolve), pause and
  ask rather than picking silently and hoping it's right.
- Verify claims against actual current code before writing them into a PR
  description, a docstring, or the final ADR — this proposal doc itself
  exists because an earlier claim ("ADR 0006 backlinks are automatic") went
  unverified for a while. Don't repeat that mistake in the other direction
  by asserting something is fixed before a real test proves it.
- Small, reviewable commits/PRs per logical concern, matching this repo's
  own commit discipline (see recent `git log` for the style — Conventional
  Commits with a gitmoji prefix).
- Full test suite (`uv run pytest -q`) and lint (`uv run ruff check .`)
  clean before considering any workstream done.
- No new tables, no new graph database or library, no agent-decided
  control flow in the shipped feature. If a design choice would require
  any of those, stop and ask instead of proceeding.

### A full live-model eval-suite run has a high baseline failure rate — don't read it as a regression signal
**Source:** session comparing `uv run pytest -m eval -q` across PRs #21-#24 and `main`, 2026-07-21

Running the complete `-m eval` suite (all skill scenarios, not a single targeted scenario) produced roughly 45-53% failures on every branch tested, including ~16-17 of 47 scenarios that failed identically across branches with zero code overlap (SCHEMA.md removal, capture-time model calls, candidate-filtering, related-notes search — none of which share a code path). Every unique-to-one-branch failure spot-checked was the same character of failure: a subjective "did the model stay strictly within its stated skill boundary" or "did it avoid inventing a disambiguating detail" rubric item, not a functional break. This matches `docs/adr/0004`'s own rationale for excluding these from the required CI gate. Before treating a full-suite eval run's failures as evidence of a regression, compare against a same-day `main` baseline (or re-run the specific failing scenario in isolation) rather than reading the raw failure count at face value — a targeted, single-scenario eval run (e.g. verifying one new rubric item after a SKILL.md wording change) is a much more reliable signal than a full-suite sweep.
